A: Because Nitro is a subscription plan, at the end of your free 3 month trial, we will start your first billing cycle so you can continue to enjoy Nitro on Discord.

However, you can cancel the Nitro subscription at any time before the end of the 3 months!

Q: Why do I see a temporary hold/charge on my account when this is supposed to be a free promotion?

A: Just to clarify, this Nitro promotion is free, however, there will be a temporary hold placed on the payment method upon activating the promotion. This is to help Discord confirm the payment method works as expected and to prevent the use of fraudulent payment methods. This charge will appear in your Discord transaction history, and it may appear as a hold on your payment method.

We immediately reverse the temporary hold, and you’ll see that reflected in your Discord transaction history. Your bank may take longer to remove the hold from your payment method.

NOTE: Banks will usually remove the temporary hold from your account within a few business days.

If your Discord transaction history does not show the hold released after 5 business days, please let us know at https://dis.gd/contact, and our support team will be able to investigate this issue further.

Potential Errors and Other Issues

Q: What if I don’t receive the email from YouTube Premium with this offer, even if I'm a YouTube Premium subscriber?

A: In order to receive this Nitro offer from YouTube, you must have opted-in for marketing emails from YouTube and be a current YouTube Premium subscriber in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, or South Korea.

If you aren’t sure how to find offers in your YouTube Premium account, follow the steps in the following link: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13365794. If you still can’t find it, contact YouTube's support team through their X page at https://x.com/TeamYouTube or at the bottom of this help article: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13365794

Q: What if I can’t find the Nitro promo in my YouTube Premium account, even if I'm a YouTube Premium subscriber?

A: In order to receive this Nitro offer from YouTube in your YouTube Premium Member Hub, you must be a current YouTube Premium subscriber in the United States. During this same period, YouTube Premium subscribers in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, and South Korea can claim their 3-month Discord Nitro offer via email.

If you aren’t sure how to find offers in your YouTube Premium account, follow the steps in the following link: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13365794. If you still can’t find it, contact YouTube's support team through their X page at https://x.com/TeamYouTube or at the bottom of this help article: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13365794

Q: I see a Sad Trombone error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link!

A: Would you happen to be entering this Nitro promo link from the YouTube premium promotion into the Discord Gift Inventory or as a link within Discord chat?

If so, this is the incorrect method for redeeming the Nitro promo link, and you will see an error when attempting to redeem the promotion.

In order to successfully claim this promotion, try opening up an incognito browser and then copy and pasting the promotion link into your browser's address bar (also known as a location bar or URL bar). 

Q: I see a "Oh no! It looks like you have Nitro already" error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link!

A: If you're seeing an "Oh no! It looks like you have Nitro already" error, that means that the Discord account you're trying to redeem this promotion on currently has a Nitro subscription so it is ineligible for this Nitro promotion.

Please make sure you're logged into the account that you want to redeem this promotion on. Or you can give the promotion link to a friend who hasn't had Nitro before!

Q: I see a "Sorry, looks like you’ve already had a Nitro sub!" error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link!

A: If you're seeing an “Sorry, looks like you’ve already had a Nitro sub” error, that means that you've previously subscribed to Nitro on your Discord account and you won't be able to redeem this 3 month perk! However, this promo link can be gifted to a friend!

If you have never subscribed to Nitro, please submit a ticket through our support system: https://dis.gd/contact and our support team will be able to investigate further.

Be sure to include your full Discord ID and email address tied to your Discord account

Q: I see a "This gift has already been redeemed" error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link!

A: If you are seeing a "This gift has been redeemed already" error, that means that the Nitro promo link has already been used and cannot be used again. You may need to double check if you've redeemed this promo link on another Discord account.

In particular, if you redeemed this promo link using your mobile device, double check the browser on your mobile device and see which Discord account you are currently logged into.

Unfortunately, once the promo link has been redeemed, the promo link cannot be re-enabled, and the Nitro cannot be transferred from one account to another.

Q: I see a "Wait a Second...Looks like this code didn't work." error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link!

A: If you're seeing an “Wait a Second...Looks like this code didn't work.” error, that means that the link is invalid! If you've copy and pasted this link, we recommend you double check the link you were given once more and make sure it exactly matches the code in your YouTube Premium Member Hub. 

If you received this link from a friend, double check with your friend on the exact link to make sure that it matches the link in their YouTube Premium account!

Please note that our support team is unable to intervene if your friend has given an invalid link and we will not be able to provide a new link.

Q: I’m having trouble with my YouTube Premium account!

A: Reach out to YouTube's support team through their X page at https://x.com/TeamYouTube or using the following link - https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13365794!

name: End-to-End Encryption for Audio and Video
title: End-to-End Encryption for Audio and Video
body:
What this article covers:
  • How to Verify that a Call is End-to-End Encrypted
  • How to Verify Participants on a Call
  • Persistent Verification Keys
  • Managing Verified Devices
  • Frequently Asked Questions

End-to-end encryption for audio and video (E2EE A/V) on Discord makes your calls even more private and secure by default. This added layer of security for audio and video calls gives visual confirmation that no one else can listen in on your calls or watch your stream besides the intended participants/viewers.

Note: All audio and video conversations in direct messages (DMs), group messages (GDMs), voice channels, and Go Live streams on Discord will soon be end-to-end encrypted by default.

Below explains how to verify that a call is end-to-end encrypted and how to confirm that the people who you are on a call with are verified too.

Note: Desktop and mobile calls between users with updated clients are end-to-end encrypted without any user action. The features described in this article do not “turn on” end-to-end encryption. We developed these features to show our work and help you confirm that our end-to-end encryption is functioning as intended.

How to Verify That a Call is End-to-End Encrypted

You can verify that your voice call on Discord is end-to-end encrypted by checking the Voice/Video Details of the call.

On the desktop app, open the Voice/Video Details in the bottom left corner of the app to see a new Privacy tab, as well as a green lock icon stating that your call is End-to-end encrypted. 

On the mobile app, you can find that green lock icon while in a voice call by pressing on the voice channel name in the top left corner of the focused voice call view.

The Privacy tab contains the Voice Privacy Code for the call. Privacy codes can be compared with other voice call participants to confirm that everyone in the call sees the same code. Comparing codes should occur out-of-band, for example on a different communication platform.

Note: Privacy codes are long so we split them up into groups of five digits to make them easier to read.

Privacy codes update when participants join or leave calls, so these codes must be compared at the same time with all current call participants in order to verify that the call is end-to-end encrypted.

Each Go Live stream associated with a call also has a Stream Privacy Code that can be accessed via the context menu for the stream, which you can find by right-clicking directly on the Go Live stream and selecting it from the dropdown menu.

By verifying the privacy code for the voice call or for any Go Live stream in the call, you can confirm that all participants have the same encrypted view of the call and that no unexpected participants have joined the call.

How to Verify Participants on a Call

Whether you’re on a call with your best friend, or a group of people in a voice channel on your favorite server, you can choose to verify the identity of the people you’re on a call with for an additional layer of privacy assurance. 

1. Navigate to “View Verification Code”. 

  1. On Desktop, right click on the user in the voice call members list or right click on their tile in the call view and select View Verification Code from the dropdown menu.
  2. On Mobile, open the user's profile either from the call member list or by long pressing on their call tile and then select View Verification Code.

2. You will then see a series of numbers that should match for both you and the person you’re on a call with. 

Note: When you show the Verification Code for another participant, you may see a warning if you have previously verified that participant and the code has changed.

3. Compare the codes out-of-band (via a different communication platform) with the person you’re speaking with.

4. If the codes are a match, then you can select Mark as Verified to confirm that you have successfully verified who you are chatting with. 

Once you’ve verified each person in the call, a small icon will appear next to their name in the call to confirm this action is complete. 

These codes are device-specific and change every time you join a new call with that person by default. With each new call, you will have to repeat the verification process. 

You can opt-in to persistent verification keys to make the verification others perform of your given device permanent. More information on how to do this in the next section.

Note: Verification Codes are long so we split them up into groups of five digits to make them easier to read.

Persistent Verification Keys

To avoid repetitive verification each time you are on a call with the same person, you can enable persistent verification keys. If you have this setting enabled, people you’re speaking with will be able to remember your device and mark it as verified. 

To enable persistent verification keys: 

1. Navigate to User Settings, then select Privacy & Safety. 

2. Select the Encryption tab, and toggle the Enable persistent verification codes

Considerations for setup: 

  • For you to save a persistent verification key for the person you’re speaking with, they’ll need to have the Enable persistent verification codes setting enabled as well.
  • Persistent verification keys are tied to your device, not your user account. This means that if both you and a friend enable this setting, you’ll remain verified to each other every time you join a voice call from those devices.
  • If you log out and back in again on your device, you will lose access to any previously used persistent verification key on that device and others who previously persistently verified your device will see that you are unverified. If you want to use persistent verification keys, you will need to enable the Enable persistent verification codes setting again.

Someone you previously persistently verified may appear unverified when:

  • They’re using a different device than the one you persistently verified
  • They had to log in again on the device you persistently verified
  • Their persistent verification key was removed from local device storage
  • They are being impersonated by someone else

Managing Verified Devices

If you have verified other users with persistent verification codes enabled, you can manage these verified devices in your User Settings.

1. Navigate to User Settings, then select Privacy & Safety. 

2. Select the Encryption tab where you’ll see Verified Devices.

a. On Desktop, select the Encryption tab.

b. On Mobile, select End-to-end Encryption under the Privacy & Safety tab.

Each user, along with their verified device(s), will be displayed. You can choose to remove the verification for a specific device, identified by the time it was verified, or remove all verifications for a specific user.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my call is end-to-end encrypted?

A: You can verify that your call is end-to-end encrypted by checking for the green End-to-end encrypted lock icon in the Voice/Video Details on the desktop app or by pressing on the voice channel name details in the top left corner of the focused call view on mobile.

Q: When will E2EE A/V roll out to Discord web and consoles?

A: Starting September 2024, all updated desktop and mobile Discord clients will support E2EE A/V. Web and consoles will receive E2EE A/V support in 2025.

Q: Why is my call not end-to-end encrypted when I’m on an updated Discord app?

A: Your call may not be end-to-end encrypted because you may be on a call with someone who is not on an updated Discord app. In 2025, all DMs, GDMs, voice channels, and Go Live streams will require updated clients that support end-to-end encryption.

Q: Can I opt out of E2EE A/V?

A: E2EE A/V is enabled by default and cannot be turned off. E2EE A/V currently won’t apply to calls where an unsupported client (i.e., web and consoles) is being used by at least one user. Stage channels also will not be end-to-end encrypted.

Q: Will the preview of my Go Live stream now be private for users not yet in the call?

A: Stream previews – when you are able to see a snippet of an ongoing Go Live stream - are NOT end-to-end encrypted. This means that users not in a call with an ongoing stream may be able to see a preview of the stream. You can disable stream previews forever, or on a per-stream basis.

Q: Can I verify the end-to-end encryption status in Go Live streams?

A: Yes, each Go Live stream has a Stream Privacy Code that can be accessed via the context menu for the stream. You can compare this code out of band with other participants to verify that the stream is end-to-end encrypted.

Q: What happens if I change my device/log into my Discord account on a new device?

A: If you change your device and have persistent verification codes enabled, you will need to go through the verification process again as verification is tied to the specific device. Persistent verification keys must be re-enabled on a new device.

name: Security Keys, Passkeys, and Passwordless Login on Discord
title: Security Keys, Passkeys, and Passwordless Login on Discord
body:
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA for short) is a great way to add an extra layer of security to your Discord account to help you stay in control of logging in.

What this article covers:
  • How to Register Passkey
    • Mobile
    • Desktop/Browser
  • Passwordless Login with Passkeys
  • How to Use Security Keys

Discord supports the newest standards for authentication: Passkeys and Security Keys, an easier to use and more secure way to sign into your account! Passkeys are encrypted digital keys you create using your fingerprint, face, or screen lock, and they can be stored in a password manager. When you log into Discord, your device will prompt you to identify yourself using a Passkey/Security Key (e.g., with Face ID), and then you’re logged in! No password needed.

All you’ll need to do is Register a Passkey. Once you’ve done that, you’re set! The next time you sign in, you’ll be able to use that passkey for one-step login - see below for more details.

How to Register Passkeys

Mobile

1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner and then tap on the cogwheel [] in the top-right corner. 

2. Tap on Account then select Security Keys. 

3. Tap Add to begin the setup process. You may be asked to confirm your password or complete an MFA challenge, if you already have one enrolled.

4. Your device will prompt you to save the passkey with a password manager. If you want more options on where to save your passkey or want to use an advanced configuration, tap Other Options.

5. Once you finish registering your key, you can choose a name for it. When you’re done, tap Finish.

6. And you’re done! Make sure to download and store your backup codes.

Desktop/Browser

1. Start by selecting the the cogwheel [] next to your username.

2. This will open your User Settings and take you to the My Account page. While here, you will be able to view the Multi-Factor Authentication options under the Password and Authentication section.

3. To set up a Security Key, select Register a Security Key and follow the prompts to reauthenticate.

4. Tap Let’s go to start the Passkey enrollment process. You’ll be prompted by your operating system, if supported, to enroll a Passkey. On MacOS, it looks like this:

 

5. After enrolling MFA, the Discord app will also have a list of backup codes for login: each of these can be used once instead of a code generated by your app, in case you lose access to it. Make sure to download and store these backup codes! If you lose these, Discord can’t help you get back into your account.

And you’re done!

You can now register another Security Key on this device or a different device (you can have up to 16 security keys/passkeys at the same time).

Passwordless Login with Passkeys

Using your passkey to log in is simple! As long as you have a password manager available with a passkey saved in it, you will be prompted to select a passkey. If you’re not getting prompted, you can always tap on Or, sign in with Passkey instead. Your system will prompt you to select the Passkey associated with your account and complete a challenge (e.g., Face ID), then you’re logged in!

How to Use Security Keys

While Security Keys function similarly to passkeys, they generally cannot be used for one-step login on Discord. Fear not! You’ll still be able to use Security Keys as a form of MFA - when you log in, you’ll get an additional challenge after entering your username and password to use you security key:

Press Authenticate with security key to interact with your Security Key, and you’re in!

Passkey Troubleshooting

Having issues with your passkey when trying to log in? Here are some troubleshooting steps to try if your passkey isn’t working for any reason:

First, try using your username and password to log in, then using your Passkey on the following MFA Challenge screen. If that doesn’t work, you’ll need to delete the existing Passkey from both your device and Discord account, then set it up once again. To do this:

1. Make sure you have your Discord backup codes handy just in case. Open your password manager and remove the passkey from your saved credentials for Discord. Refer to your password manager’s documentation for details on how to do this.

2. Use a different MFA method or device to complete the challenge. If you don’t have another set up, you can use a backup code from the list you saved to complete the MFA challenge and finish the login.

3. Go to your Account Settings and repeat the enrollment process to register a new passkey with your password manager. See How to Register Passkeys above for more details, and be sure to remember what you name it!

4. From the Account Settings screen, delete the old passkey associated with your Discord account.

And now you’re starting fresh! Following these steps ensures your remaining saved backup codes continue to work while enrolling a new Passkey.

name: Discord and Amazon Music Connection FAQ
title: Discord and Amazon Music Connection FAQ
body:
What this article covers: 

  • How to Launch Amazon Music Activity 
  • How to Troubleshoot “Failed to Connect” Error
  • How to Delete an Amazon Music Connection 
    • Via Discord on Desktop
    • Through Amazon’s Website or App

How to Launch Amazon Music Activity

Note: An Amazon account and Amazon Music Unlimited subscription is required to use the Amazon Music Activity.

1. To launch the Amazon Music Activity, navigate to a voice channel or text channel:

  • Via a voice channel: Press the Activity Launcher [] and select the Amazon Music Activity. 

  •  Via a text channel on desktop: Press the App Launcher [] button located right of the chat bar option. Then, select the Amazon Music Activity. 

  • Via text channels on mobile: Press the App Launcher [] button next to the chat bar. Then, select the Amazon Music Activity.

2. Once launched, you will need to provide authorization if you’ve never launched your chosen Activity before.

3. Then, be sure to sign in to your Amazon account or create an account by pressing Sign in. This will redirect you to Amazon via browser. 

4. Once you have successfully connected, close the web browser and return back to the Activity in Discord. 

If you do not have an Amazon Music Unlimited subscription, you will be asked to subscribe. If you have an Amazon Music Unlimited subscription, the Activity should load and you can start listening to music!

How to Troubleshoot “Failed to Connect” Error

If you are running into a “Failed to Connect” error while connecting to the Amazon Music Activity, follow the troubleshooting steps below: 

1. Verify that you have a reliable and strong internet connection. 

2. Ensure that the Amazon account you’re using is not already linked to another Discord account. Each Amazon account can only be connected to one Discord account at a time.

3. In Discord, head into your User Settings > Connections and check if you have previously connected to Amazon Music. 

a. If you are not connected, please retry connecting to Amazon Music. 

b. If you are connected, delete the Amazon Music connection via Discord and Amazon.com by following the steps below. 

4. Make sure your Discord desktop app or mobile app is up-to-date.

5. Force quit the Discord app, and try the steps again.

6. If you continue to experience connection issues, attempt the troubleshooting steps on another platform or device. For example, if you encounter problems on Discord's mobile app, try following the steps using the desktop application. This can help isolate whether the issue is specific to a particular platform or device. 

How to Delete an Amazon Music Connection

Via Discord on Desktop

1. To delete your Amazon Music connection, head into your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel [] in the lower-left corner. 

2. Then, navigate to Connections, where you'll find your Amazon Music connection if you’ve previously linked it. 

3. To delete the connection, select the x button in the upper-right corner of the Activity and Disconnect.

Through Amazon’s Website or App

1. Go to Amazon.com and sign into your Amazon account. 

2. Then, navigate to Account > Manage your data. 

3. Once in Manage your data, select Manage apps & services with data access. If you’ve previously connected to Discord, you will see the Discord app listed. 

4. To delete the connection, press Remove in the Manage Connection column. 

If you have additional questions or encounter any issues with the Activity or Connections, please reach out to our Support team here.

And that’s it! Enjoy sharing and listening to sweet tunes with your friends.

name: ICYMI (In Case You Missed It) FAQs
title: ICYMI (In Case You Missed It) FAQs
body:
Note: This feature is currently experimental. It is only available to a limited number of English, US users on the iOS mobile app.

What this article covers:

  • What is ICYMI?
  • How to edit which Servers or Channels appear in your ICYMI
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is ICYMI?

The ICYMI (or In Case You Missed It) tab allows you to catch up on server messages, activities, and more that you might have missed while you weren’t actively using Discord. 

Your ICYMI tab will display recently played activity from friends, status updates, messages and announcements from servers, conversation summaries and more! Some summaries may be generated with the help of AI.

How to edit which Servers or Channels appear in your ICYMI

If there is a specific server or channel that you want to see more or less of in your ICYMI feed, you can make adjustments through the settings on the ICYMI tab. 

1. While in the ICYMI tab, tap on the filters icon [] in the top-right corner. 

2. Tap on Adjust Server/Channel Recommendations.

3. Pick which server you want to make adjustments for by tapping on it.

4. You can completely remove a server from displaying in your ICYMI feed by toggling Show content in ICYMI, or you can adjust how much information from a server is displayed on ICYMI by selecting one of the following:

  • See Less: You will see less content from this server.
  • Good As Is: With this selected your settings will stay the same.
  • See More!: You will see more content from this server.

5. If you tap on a specific channel, you can edit these settings for each channel, or toggle Show content in ICYMI to completely disable this channel from showing. 

6. You can review each server and adjust the settings based on your preferences. 

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why is my ICYMI feed empty?

A: When you first access the ICYMI tab, it may take up to 5 minutes for your first feed to generate and it may take 30 minutes for content to be available from all your servers.

Q: Is this feature only available on the mobile app?

A: Yes, ICYMI is only available on the iOS version of our mobile application.

Q: Can I disable ICYMI?

A: Yes. Tap on your avatar in the bottom-right corner. Then tap on the cogwheel [] in the top-right to access User Settings. Press on Advanced and then tap the toggle next to Hide ICYMI tab at the bottom.

name: Ads Policy
title: Ads Policy
body:
Overview

All advertising content is subject to Discord’s community guidelines, however there are additional restrictions for advertising content. 

Discord’s Ads Policy, outlined below, provides guidance to advertisers on the platform to publish trustworthy, safe, useful, and high-quality ads to users. Ads are prohibited, restricted, or allowed based on Discord’s content policies below. 

  • Prohibited: Content you cannot advertise.
  • Restricted: Content you can advertise, with limitations.
  • Allowed: Content you can advertise.

In this policy, you will also find our ads practices and our editorial guidelines for designing and implementing your ad copy and landing page.

This policy is mandatory and applies to all native and third party ads on Discord including ads in Activities. The policy applies to the ad, the landing page, the username, reward, and any other surface directly associated with the ad.

Advertisers on Discord are responsible for their ads ensuring they follow all applicable laws and regulations. In addition to Discord's Ads Policy, advertisers must comply with our Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, and all other policies governing the use of our services.

Ads Content Policy

Below are examples of ads content that is prohibited or restricted on Discord.

Adult Sexual Content

Discord prohibits the promotion of explicit and implicit adult sexual content.

Adult sexual content includes depiction of, or references to:

  • Compensated sexual acts (e.g. escort services, cuddling sites, intimate massage, sex work),
  • Full or partial nudity,
  • Mail-order brides or international marriage brokers,
  • Models in sexualized poses,
  • Non-consensual sexual themes,
  • Penis enlargement or breast enhancement,
  • Pornography, cartoon porn, or hentai,
  • Products in the shape of intimate body parts (e.g. genitals, butts, female breasts),
  • Reproductive, contraceptive, or fertility products,
  • Sex toys and personal lubricants, 
  • Strip and host/hostess clubs,
  • Suggestive live chat or phone calls,
  • Other explicit or implicit suggestive content.

Alcohol Content

Discord prohibits alcohol advertising including branding, online and offline sale, and consumption of alcoholic beverages. 

Alcohol advertising includes:

  • Sale of any type of alcoholic beverage (e.g., beer, wine, or liquor),
  • Events sponsored by alcohol brands,
  • Competitions where alcohol is a prize,
  • Non-alcoholic products offered by alcohol brands,
  • Simulated alcohol games,
  • Depicting people under the influence,
  • Hangover treatments.

Body Alteration

Discord prohibits advertising of body-altering products and services.

Body Alteration includes:

  • Invasive cosmetic procedures (e.g. tongue splitting, ear shaping, waist training),
  • Body piercing,
  • Permanent tattoos,
  • Permanent makeup,
  • UV Skin tanning or skin bleaching products and services.

Charitable Causes

Discord restricts the solicitation of funds for or promotion of charitable causes. Soliciting funds or donations is only allowed for tax-exempt organizations. The ad or ad’s destination must clearly state that donations are tax-exempt, or disclose a charity number or a tax exemption number.

The following are allowed:

  • In the United States, organizations that have 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status,
  • Entities with an equivalent non-profit registration in their home country.

The following are prohibited:

  • Soliciting funds on behalf of a politician, political party, or any other violation of the political content policy,
  • Soliciting funds without tax-exempt status.

Children’s Content 

Discord prohibits advertisements intended solely for children. Children’s content is defined as any content intended for an audience below 13 which is Discord’s minimum age requirement.

Examples of Children's content include:

  • Activities that appeal to children, such as play-acting, simple songs or games, or early education,
  • Actors, characters, celebrities, or toys that appeal to children, including animated characters or cartoon figures.
  • Songs, poems, stories, or other subject matter that reflect an intent to target children.

This policy does not apply to general audience content that could appeal to everyone, but isn’t intended specifically for children, and/or content that is intended for those 13 years or older. 

Dating

Discord prohibits ads for online dating apps or services, matchmaking services, or romance coaching.

Dangerous Activities

Discord prohibits ads that depict or encourage real world dangerous activities.

Dangerous activities create an extreme risk of physical harm to the participant including but not limited to:

  • Physical challenge or stunt trends,
  • Misuse of fireworks.

Drugs and Drugs Paraphernalia

Discord prohibits advertisement of illegal or recreational drugs and paraphernalia.

Drugs and drugs paraphernalia advertising includes but is not limited to:

  • Illegal drugs,
  • Recreational and herbal drugs,
  • CBD products,
  • Accessories associated with drug use and storage (e.g. grinders, syringes, pipes),
  • Drug dispensaries, 
  • Depictions of intoxication or drug use.

Financial Products and Services

Discord prohibits the promotion of financial products and services.

Prohibited financial products and services include but is not limited to:

  • Banking services and institutions,
  • Buy now, pay later (BNPL) providers and payment installment services,
  • Currency exchange, trading, and services,
  • Cryptocurrency and related products
  • Contract for Difference (CFDs),
  • Debt relief and consolidation,
  • Digital wallets,
  • Insurance,
  • Loans products and services,
  • Mobile and electronic payments,
  • Mortgage services,
  • Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and related products,
  • Securities,
  • Tax preparation or filing.

Gambling Content

Discord prohibits the promotion of gambling or gambling-adjacent activities.

The following are prohibited:

  • Affiliates and websites driving traffic to gambling,
  • Brick-and-mortar casinos,
  • Online casinos and gambling,
  • Odds, tips, picks, forecasts, and handicapping, 
  • Gambling advice and discussions,
  • Games or apps played for money,
  • Horse race betting,
  • Lotteries,
  • Pay to play games of chance with prizes of real-world value,
  • Simulated casinos and their games,
  • Sports betting, sports books, or fantasy sports.

Hateful Content

Discord prohibits ads that promote hateful content.

Hateful content includes degrading, mocking, threatening, attacking or advocating against individuals or protected groups based on, but not limited to:

  • Race,
  • Ethnicity,
  • National origin,
  • Color,
  • Sex,
  • Sexual orientation,
  • Gender identity, 
  • Religious affiliation,
  • Age,
  • Physical or mental disability,
  • Medical or genetic condition,
  • Veteran status,
  • Refugee status,
  • Immigrant Status,
  • Familial status.

Healthcare Content

Discord prohibits advertisement of healthcare products and services. 

Prohibited healthcare products and services include:

  • Clinical trials,
  • Surrogacy services,
  • Telemedicine providers,
  • Online pharmacy,
  • Prescription medicines,
  • Mental health services,
  • Rehabilitation centers,
  • Over the Counter (OTC) medicines, 
  • Health and dietary supplements,
  • Medical devices,
  • Surgical and non surgical cosmetic procedures (e.g. lip fillers, botox, skin lightening creams, plastic surgery). 

Illegal Products and Services

Discord prohibits advertising of illegal products and services, including anything that facilitates or promotes illegal behavior.

Illegal products and services include but is not limited to:

  • Fake IDs, passports, or other official documents,
  • Illegal streaming or downloading of copyrighted material,
  • Instructions for or equipment to illegally access websites, cell phones or software.  

Inappropriate Content

Discord prohibits advertising that contains inappropriate content. 

Categories Discord considers to be inappropriate content include:

  • Distasteful content
    • Content meant to shock or scare,
    • Imagery of guts, gore, sexual fluids, human or animal waste.
  • Offensive and divisive content
  • Sensitive events
    • Content that refers to a sensitive event or topic (e.g. deaths, natural disasters, violent attacks, civil disorder) and contains personal attacks, the selling of goods or services, solicitation of followers, or other attempts to capitalize on these events.
  • Misinformation
    • Content that is false including disinformation, conspiracy theories, and climate change denial.
  • Misleading synthetic or manipulated content
  • Profanity and vulgarity
    • Including obscene uses of symbols, emojis, or gestures.
  • Personal attacks
    • Including the use of non-public personal information in ads.
  • Violence
    • Graphic imagery and realistic displays of crime, violence, physical trauma, execution, 
    • Excessive gore, physical or psychological abuse, self-harm, animal abuse or torture.
  • Malware & Software Downloads
    • The advertising of malware products, including software or devices such as VPN promoting access to geo blocked or illegal services.
    • Malware products include but is not limited to:
      • Spyware,
      • Stalkerware,
      • Illegal hacking devices,
      • Phishing links,
      • Software that is deceptive or compromises user safety.

Intellectual Property

Discord prohibits ads that infringe the copyright, intellectual property, trademark, privacy, or other legal rights of any person or entity.

The following are prohibited:

  • References to Discord and uses of Discord-owned trademark, including suggestions of affiliation with or endorsement by Discord,
  • Ads for products or services primarily used to infringe the intellectual property rights of others,
  • Ads for products or services primarily dedicated to selling counterfeit products,
  • Use of the name, likeness, voice, or other identifying features of an individual without consent,
  • Any use of copyrighted material without written permission.

Political Content

Discord prohibits advertising that contains political content.

Political content includes but is not limited to references to a:

  • Candidate,
  • Political party,
  • Political Action Committees (PACs) or Super PACs,
  • Elected or appointed government official, 
  • Election or referendum, 
  • Ballot measure, proposition, legislation, regulation, or judicial outcome.
  • Advocacy for or against any of the above. 

Tobacco and Tobacco Accessories

Discord prohibits the advertising of tobacco products or accessories. 

Prohibited tobacco products include but are not limited to:

  • Tobacco of any kind,
  • Hookah,
  • Cigars and cigarettes,
  • Cigar bars and hookah lounges,
  • Imitation smoking,
  • Pipes, rolling papers, or filters,
  • E-cigarettes, e-liquid, or vapes.

Unacceptable Business Practices

Discord prohibits unacceptable business models, products, and services.

Categories Discord considers to be unacceptable business practices include but is not limited to:

  • Animal or insect sale,
  • Bail bonds,
  • Counterfeit goods or services, 
  • Homework or essay writing services for students,
  • Extortion and blackmail,
  • Multi-level marketing models or get-rich-quick schemes,
  • Payday loans,
  • Services attempting to change an individual's sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression,
  • Selling social media followers,
  • False, unsubstantiated, unrealistic, or exaggerated claims,
  • Deceptive or misleading ads which withhold reasonable information on pricing, terms or expenses from the landing page. 

Weapons and Weapons Accessories

Discord prohibits the advertising of real-world weapons and weapons accessories.  

Prohibited real-world weapons and weapons accessories include but are not limited to:

  • Knives, throwing stars, daggers, spears, or swords,
  • Guns, firearms, airsoft guns, air guns, blow guns, paintball guns, antique guns, replica guns, imitation guns, or gun parts,
  • Stun guns, taser guns, mace, pepper spray, or other weapons of self defense,
  • Bombs, fireworks, flamethrowers, gunpowder, or explosives,
  • Weapon making instructions,
  • Weapon training programs or classes,
  • Ammunition.

This policy does not apply to ads of virtual reality weapons and weapons accessories for use in video games. 

Weight loss Products and Services

Discord prohibits the advertising of diet and weight loss products and services.

Prohibited diet and weight loss products and services include but are not limited to:

  • Weight loss language or imagery,
  • Diet or weight loss testimonials,
  • Weight loss or appetite suppressant pills or supplements,
  • Before and after weight loss imagery,
  • Procedures such as liposuction, fat burning, or cool sculpting,
  • Encouragement or glamorization of unhealthy or unsafe eating behaviors or eating disorders.

This policy does not apply to ads that promote health, wellness, and fitness products and services that do not focus on weight loss.

Campaign Considerations

Targeting

In order to protect user experience on the platform, advertisers are prohibited from targeting ads to certain audiences or using sensitive categories for such ad targeting. 

Advertisers are prohibited from: 

  • Using copy that asserts or implies knowledge of a user's personally identifiable information. Personally identifiable information (PII) includes any information that could be used to identify an individual, such as a name, home address, social security number, banking information, driver's license number, and any other sensitive data.
  • Targeting users based on any of the following categories: 
    • Alleged or actual commission of a crime 
    • Health 
    • Negative financial status or condition 
    • Marital or relationship status
    • Race, color, or ethnic origin 
    • Religious or philosophical affiliation and/or beliefs 
    • Sexual orientation 
    • Gender identities other than cisgender 
    • Political affiliation and/or beliefs 
    • Trade union membership 
    • Genetic and/or biometric data

In addition to these targeting restrictions, ads for housing or employment are not allowed to target users based on age, sex, gender, or precise location (post code or more precise location). 

Editorial Guidelines

To keep ads trustworthy and useful for Discord users, ads and their landing page must meet our editorial criteria for accuracy and quality. 

Accuracy:

  • Ads must represent the brand or product being advertised.
  • Ads must not be misleading or make exaggerated, sensationalized or inaccurate claims.

Quality:

  • Text must use correct grammar and spelling 
  • Text must avoid excessive punctuation, spaces, or symbols.
  • Images, video, and audio must not be unclear, indecipherable, fuzzy, blurry, extremely grainy, or otherwise of low quality.
  • Imagery with artificial functionality is not permitted (e.g. play or download buttons, notification icons, or elements that mimic Discord features).
  • Images and video must be oriented correctly (not sideways or upside down).

Landing Page:

  • The destination URL must link to a functional landing page.
  • The landing page's primary purpose must not be for advertising and must be relevant to what is being promoted in the ad.
  • The landing page must not contain intrusive pop-up ads, automatic downloads, redirect users to another site, or require users to sign in before they can view the page.
  • The contents of the landing page must comply with all of Discord’s ads content policies.

Sanctions

Advertisements that violate US or other applicable sanctions are prohibited on Discord. 

Additionally, advertisements may not be targeted to individuals located in regions that are subject to general embargoes or comprehensive trade restrictions.

name: File Attachments FAQ
title: File Attachments FAQ
body:
What this article covers:
  • What is a File Attachment?
  • How to Attach Files
  • File Upload Settings
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • What is NSFW Content Scanning?
  • How to Use Alt Text

What is a File Attachment?

In addition to text messages, users can upload file attachments in Discord to send to others. If you have Nitro, you can upload even bigger files. For non-Nitro subscribers, the maximum file upload is 10MB. 

There is a wide variety of file types that can be uploaded to Discord. Here are the most common examples:

  • JPEG
  • PDF
  • MOV
  • MP4
  • MP3

How to Attach Files

Note: If you upload multiple video files, images, or GIFs in one message, they will be sent together and displayed as a mosaic format.

1. Tap on the plus sign [] located in the text field of the text channel, text chat of a voice channel, or group message that you want to send a file attachment in and then tap on Upload a File.

2. Select the file(s) that you want to attach from your device. You can also write a message to send along with it. 

3. Your file(s) and any text that you included will be sent together in one message.

If you attach non-image files, such as a PDF, DOC, etc.  the files will display as embeds in your message and will not provide a preview of the attached file.

Note: If you want to include Spoiler Tags before sending a file to someone, you can learn how to do that in this Help Center article.

File Upload Settings

There are some settings you can enable to prevent or even minimize the attachments you'll see in Discord.

Desktop/Browser

1. Tap on the cogwheel [] in the bottom-left corner of the app.

2. Navigate to the Chat tab. 

3. A setting is enabled if there’s a checkmark or a setting is disabled if there’s an x.

Here is how each setting works:

  • When posted as links to chat: When an image is posted as a link, the image will be displayed instead of the text link.
  • When uploaded directly to Discord: Any image that is larger than 10MB will be shared as a download instead.
  • With image descriptions: Used for screen readers to describe any shared image.
  • Show embeds and preview website links pasted into the chat: Embeds and website links will display a preview, unless disabled.

Mobile

1. Tap on your profile image in the bottom-right corner.

2. Press on the cogwheel [] in the top-right corner.

3. Navigate to the Chat tab. 

4. On this page, you can enable or disable any setting. If enabled, you’ll see a checkmark. If disabled, you’ll see an x.

5. A lot of the settings on Desktop/Browser are the same for mobile, but let’s go over the mobile-only settings:

  • Save to Device: If you directly send an image or video through your mobile device, the file will be automatically saved to your phone.
  • Video Uploads: In this section, you can manage the quality of videos you upload through Discord. By selecting the "Data Saver" option, your videos will upload more quickly and consume less data.
  • Data Saving Mode: If enabled, images and videos will be sent in lower quality through your cellular network to use less data.

What is NSFW Content Scanning?

"NSFW" or Not Safe For Work (or not suitable for work) is a term to describe inappropriate content that you wouldn't want to look at while in the workplace and is now more widely used to describe content that could be seen as inappropriate for the public.

To help keep users safe, we have both a user and server setting to scan images for NSFW content. If the setting is enabled and the system detects the image could be NSFW, it will block the upload.

You can learn more about these settings in our Safer Messaging on Discord Help Center article.

How to Use Alt Text

Note: ALT text can’t be added to an image if it has already been uploaded.

ALT text - short for alternative text - is a feature that allows users to write an image description to uploads so that anyone using a screen reader can obtain a description of the image without needing to see the actual image itself. 

1. Once you attach the image(s) you want to upload, tap on the pencil icon [] that appears after hovering your cursor over each file.

2. You can change the name of the file and add in the ALT text to describe the image. Press on Save when you’re finished. 

3. You can now send your image(s) with the alt text you’ve written. 

4. If you have the With image descriptions setting enabled and if an image has ALT text, you should see the word ALT on the image. Select ALT and you will then see the ALT text for the image.

If an image has ALT text, you'll be able to see it when you have With image descriptions enabled in your Text & Images settings. If you need a visual aid, pressing ALT this will show the text.

Congratulations! You now have the skills to upload images, send files, and perform other actions through Discord.

name: Discover Tab
title: Discover Tab
body:
Note: This feature is currently experimental and available to only a percentage of users on desktop and mobile.
What this article covers:
  • Discover Tab
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • Servers
  • Quests
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Discover Tab

The Discover tab is a central place for finding things to do on Discord. Here, users can discover servers, Quests, and much more. 

Desktop

To navigate to the Discover tab on desktop, select the Discover icon [] at the bottom of the server list on the left side of the app.

This will direct you to the Discover page where you can explore the category pages.

How to Navigate to the Discover Tab on Desktop

Mobile

On mobile, select the Discover icon [] at the bottom of the app.

How to Navigate to the Discover Tab on Mobile

Servers

The search option in the Servers tab is currently available only on desktop and not on mobile devices during the experimental phase.

Servers in Discord are virtual spaces where communities gather to chat, share content, and interact. You can learn more about Server Discovery here.

In the Discover Tab, you will find discoverable Community Servers along with their categories.

To take a closer look at these communities, select the Servers tab within the Discover tab.

  

Servers Tab: Desktop (Left) and Mobile (Right) in Discover

In Servers, you can browse various server categories like gaming, music, entertainment, and more by selecting from the category bar located at the top of the Servers page.

 

Browsing Server Categories in Discover: Desktop (Left) and Mobile (Right). Servers are sorted into relevant categories and order of popularity based on the server’s member count.

When you’re ready, press the server you would like to preview! 

Quests

Quests are a way for players to discover games and earn rewards for playing them on Discord. Whether you are playing or streaming your favorite game on Discord, you now have a chance to get rewards!
To explore available Discord Quests, select the Quest tab within the Discover list.

 

Quests Tab in Discover: Desktop (Left) and Mobile (Right)

In Quests, you can view recent and current Discord Quests from the last 30 days. While here, press Accept Quest for active Quests to begin.

  

“Accept Quest” Button: Desktop (Left) and Mobile (Right)

You can also see past Quests that you’ve completed and earned rewards for by selecting Claimed Quests within the category bar located at the top of the Quest page.

The Claimed Quests category is available only on desktop.

Claimed Quests Category on Desktop

Start a Quest today and enjoy the rewards! You can learn more about Discord Quests here. 

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why was my server recently removed from Discover?

A: If your server was recently removed from the Discover tab, it may be due to a violation of Discord’s Discovery Guidelines. Please review the Discord Server Discovery Guidelines and ensure your server complies with them.

name: [Known Issue] Game Overlay
title: [Known Issue] Game Overlay
body:
We have paid attention to user feedback regarding the reliability of Discord’s Game Overlay, which has been known to occasionally cause problems during gameplay. Moreover, it is only supported in a limited number of games due to compatibility challenges inherent to the current implementation.

As a result, on April 15, 2024, Discord started to roll-out a revamped Game Overlay designed to significantly enhance stability, reliability, and performance. The new Game Overlay will not interfere with your game, and is expected to be compatible with nearly all games. This is currently out to 100% of users on the Canary and PTB versions of the Discord app. There is no ETA at this time as to when this will be fully rolled out to all users on the Stable version of Discord.

After this date, you will experience the following changes in Game Overlay behavior:

  • Game Overlay is now enabled by default for all games.
  • Game Overlay will work in windowed fullscreen mode and windowed borderless fullscreen mode, but will not work in true fullscreen mode.
    • True fullscreen mode on desktop means that other computer applications cannot be displayed over the application that’s in true fullscreen mode.
  • Game Overlay will be hidden when the game window is not in focus.
  • Screensharing the game window will not capture the Game Overlay, but screensharing the full screen will still capture the Game Overlay.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What do I do if I always run my game in true fullscreen mode?

A: Most games support borderless fullscreen mode, so you can switch to this mode to continue getting Discord’s Game Overlay in game.

If you need to run the game in true fullscreen mode for any reason, there’s also a global Enable legacy overlay option in User Settings > Game Overlay. Please note that this option may be removed in the future.



Q: Can I keep using the legacy Game Overlay?
A: You can continue using it as long as the option exists in the app, but our goal is to eventually move everyone over to the revamped Game Overlay so they can enjoy a more stable and performant experience.

Q: What if the game I play only works with the legacy Game Overlay?

A: Please first check that you are running borderless fullscreen mode, or sometimes called “windowed” fullscreen mode. The revamped Game Overlay should work in this mode.

If you still experience issues with it, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance.

title: 1 Month of Nitro for Customers of Select Western Digital Products
body:
Starting from August 1, 2024, Western Digital customers can claim 1 month of Discord Nitro from purchasing eligible Western Digital products. Learn below about how you can claim Discord Nitro.

Promotion Summary

Offer Details: 1 month of Discord Nitro

Who is Eligible: Users who have had an active Nitro membership or Nitro trial in the last 12 months are not eligible to redeem this Nitro promotion.

Users who have had a Discord Nitro membership at any point on their accounts and have had a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic membership in the past 12 months are ineligible to redeem this promotion.

If a user has had a Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting membership active on their account and they’ve never had a Nitro membership, redeeming this promotion will override that membership.

We will not be able to refund any leftover membership time from those, and the user will be forfeiting the remainder of the existing membership when activating the 1 month Nitro trial.

Users who have already claimed a gift from this promotion are not eligible to claim further gifts from this promotion.

This promotion is only available in certain regions where Discord Nitro and eligible Western Digital products are available. If you receive an "Unknown Gift Code" error during the claim/redemption process, you are not eligible to redeem this promotion. You can learn more at this Help Center article.

Requirements: Claim the promo by purchasing eligible Western Digital products starting August 1, 2024, and redeem it in your Discord account by July 17, 2026.

NOTE: This promo is only available to customers who have purchased Western Digital products with eligible SKUs. 

Membership: After the 1 month trial period, your Nitro membership will convert to a monthly recurring membership, and Discord will bill your payment method for per month until you cancel it. You can cancel at any time in your Discord User Settings.

    • Step by Step Redeem Instructions

  • Frequently Asked Questions
    • Promotion Details
