name: Managing Subscriptions and Billing FAQ
title: Managing Subscriptions and Billing FAQ
body:
What this article covers: 

    • Where to Manage all of Your Active Subscriptions 
    • Billing Information and History
      • How do I add or edit payment methods?
      • How do I change my payment methods for my subscription?
      • How do I remove a payment method?
      • Where can I download my tax invoice or purchase receipt?
    • What payment methods are accepted?
    • What Discord Purchases Will Look Like on Your Statement
    • Frequently Asked Questions

Where to Manage all of Your Active Subscriptions 

When you’ve purchased a Nitro subscription, or maybe added some Server Boosts to your account, you can manage those subscriptions and find information about them in your Subscriptions. 

1. Head into your User Settings by pressing the cogwheel [] icon. 

2. Then, select the Subscriptions tab.

Once there, you can find information about:

  • Any active subscriptions;
  • The renewal dates and amounts you'll be charged;
  • Options to manage your subscriptions, including canceling or switching plans; 
  • Any gift subscription credits you’ve received.

For more information on how to cancel a subscription, please check out one of these relevant articles depending on your subscription type: Nitro subscription, Server Boosting, Server subscription, or Premium App.

Billing Information and History

You can find your payment methods on file, as well as your payment history, under User Settings > Billing. 

How do I add or edit payment methods?

You can add a new payment method or edit any pre-existing payment methods in the Billing tab. 

To add a payment method, select the Add Payment Method button and complete the prompts.

If you would like to make changes to a pre-existing payment method, select the Edit button to the right of the payment method. From there, you will be able to view the payment method information.

You can also set a payment method as default. The default payment method will be the first payment method that appears when making new purchases. To select which payment method shows as default:

1. Select Edit next to the payment method you’d like to set as the default, or Add a new payment method.

2. Select Make this my default payment method at the bottom.

3. Press Save. 

How do I change my payment method for my subscription?

You can find the payment method associated with any subscriptions in User Settings > Subscriptions. This section will show the payment method you first purchased a subscription with. 

If you’d like to change the payment method for your ongoing subscription payments:

1. Open User Settings > Subscriptions.

2. Find the Pay for it With section.

3. Select a payment method.

Note: Updating your subscription payment method does not automatically change which payment method is set as your default payment method. If you’d like to set one card as both your default and subscription payment methods, you will need to update both settings to the same card. 

If you have a Nitro or Boost subscription, the payment method set under the Pay for it With section will show a corresponding Subscription tag under User Settings > Billing. 

How do I remove a payment method?

1. To remove a payment method, head over to your User Settings > Billing. 

2. Then, select Edit located to the right of the payment method. 
3. While reviewing your payment method details, select Delete Payment Method to remove it.

Note: If you have an active subscription, we require you to have at least one saved payment method. If you’d like to cancel your subscription and remove your cards on file, be sure to cancel your subscription first.

Where can I download my tax invoice or purchase receipt?

1. You can locate either your purchase receipt or tax invoice by heading into your User Settings > Billing. 

2. Then, select a transaction within your Transaction History to review your Purchase Details. 

3. Within your Purchase Details, depending on which document you have available, you will see  Download Tax Invoice or Download extended purchase receipt > Download PDF. Once the download is complete, you will be able to review the document.

You may see either the “Download extended purchase receipt" or "Download tax invoice” within this section. 

What payment methods are accepted?

To make a purchase, you will need a valid payment method linked to your account. 

We currently accept the following payment methods:

  • A valid credit/debit card (Global)
  • PayPal (Global)
  • Apple Pay
  • Google Pay
  • Venmo (United States)
  • Paysafecard (Germany)
  • Gcash (Philippines)
  • Grabpay (Malaysia)
  • MoMoWallet (Vietnam)
  • KakaoPay (South Korea)
  • iDEAL (Netherlands)
  • Bancontact (Belgium)
  • EPS (Austria)
  • Przelewy24 (Poland)
  • GoPay (Indonesia)

Note: When selecting your payment method, please note we are unable to provide refunds for purchases made with Paysafecards.

What Discord Purchases Will Look Like on Your Statement

The deed has been done and you completed your purchase, now if you were at all curious how it’ll look like on your bank statements end, it should look like the below!

Here is what you will see if you made a purchase with a Credit/Debit card directly:

Here is what you will see if you made a purchase via PayPal:

Note: All purchases made within Discord will be labeled DISCORD*ItemName within credit/debit card statements depending on how your bank renders this and PAYPAL* DISCORD if completed through PayPal. If you would like a refund for any purchases, check out our refund policy here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: My payments are failing, and/or I see pending transactions in my bank statement. What should I do?

A: Visit our Help Center article to learn more about how to handle failed payments. 

Q: I want to remove all my payment methods, but I can't. What's going on?

A: Removing payment methods does not end a subscription for you. In order to remove all payment methods, you will need to cancel any remaining active subscriptions first. Visit our Help Center article here for how to cancel your subscriptions.

Q: What does “proration” mean?

A: Proration for a subscription means adjusting the cost based on how much of the subscription period you've used. Discord uses this to ensure you’re being charged the correct amount when adding subscriptions or removing subscriptions on your account, and in situations like when accepting a special offer or discount. 

Q: I have a Nitro Monthly subscription, but I just purchased a Nitro Yearly subscription. Can I get a refund? 

A: Your original Nitro Monthly subscription was used as proration credit toward your Nitro Yearly subscription upgrade. This means the amount you paid for Nitro Yearly was not the full amount as you paid the prorated charge. When the subscription renews, you will be charged the full price of the subscription. To check your receipt, check User Settings > Billing. 

Q: What’s the difference between the default payment method and my subscription payment method? 

A: The default payment method determines which payment will show first when making new purchases on Discord. However, your subscription payment method is what’s used to pay for your recurring Nitro and Boost subscriptions.
You can set the same payment method for both by following the steps to update your default payment method and updating your subscription payment method.   

Please note that the payment method used to pay for server and app subscriptions specifically will not show a Subscription tag within the Billing tab, and these subscriptions will charge from either the original payment method selected or the payment method set for the specific App subscription in the Premium App Subscriptions list.

Q: What happens if I previously purchased a Server Boost subscription, and now I’m buying an additional Nitro Yearly subscription?

A: If you have purchased any additional subscription with a different billing cycle, Discord will unify all of your subscription payment dates. This means that your subscription type may change from a monthly cycle to a yearly cycle if you have purchased additional subscriptions with a yearly cycle.

Additionally, if you purchase an application or server subscription, your Server Boost subscription cycle won't be affected.

For example, if you initially had a Server Boost Monthly subscription, purchasing an additional  Nitro Yearly subscription will convert the current Server Boost Monthly subscription to a Server Boost Yearly subscription in order to simplify all subscription charges to one payment date.

Q: When making a purchase, I see something called “adjustments.” What is this?

A: Adjustments can be added to a purchase for a few reasons when signing up for additional subscription purchases, such as:  

  • If you're changing your billing plan from monthly to yearly
  • If your payment is being prorated
  • If you are getting a discount

Q: I’m receiving a “Billing address is invalid” error when making purchase. How do I fix this?

A: If you see this error while attempting to make a purchase, this means that the billing address associated with the card you are trying to use does not match the address filed with your bank. Please check User Settings > Billing > Select the card > Edit and update your billing address. 

Q: Why do I still have server boosts when I canceled my Nitro subscription? 

A: Server Boosts are a separate monthly subscription, and it's possible that you have one or more Server Boost subscriptions active. To manage the subscription, you would need to go to your User Settings > Subscriptions. 

Q: I have a new Discord account, can I transfer my Nitro subscription to another account?
A: Unfortunately, Discord doesn't currently support transferring Nitro subscriptions between accounts. We understand this might be a bit inconvenient, and we appreciate your understanding.

name: Friends List 101
title: Friends List 101
body:
What this article covers:
  • What is the Friends List?
  • How to Add a User to Your Friends List
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • How to Accept or Decline a Friend Request
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile

What is the Friends List?

The friends list is your list of all of the friends that you have added on Discord. Here is everything you can see under the Friends tab: 

  • All: All of your added friends.
  • Online: Your friends who are currently online or idle.
  • Pending: Friend requests you’ve received and sent. You can also view spam requests by tapping the View spam requests sub-section.
  • Blocked: Users you've chosen to block. 

How to Add a User to Your Friends List

Desktop/Browser

Option 1

1. Tap on the Direct Messages icon in the upper-left corner of the app. Then select the Friends tab. 

 

2. Press Add Friend to add a friend. Input their username in the text field and press Send Friend Request to send the request. If the username is not entered correctly, you will receive an error. Otherwise, you can check under Pending to see the pending request.

Option 2

1. While in a server, group message, or direct message (DM), tap on the profile of the user  you’d like to add as a friend.

2. Tap the Add Friend icon [ ]  to send a friend request.

Mobile

Option 1

1. Tap the  Messages icon [] in the top-left corner of the mobile app.

2. Then tap Add Friends.

3.  Add a friend using any of the listed methods, or select Add by Username to input their username.

4. Once you’ve entered the username, press Send Friend Request.

Option 2

1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner and navigate to your friends list by tapping on Your Friends.

2. In the top-right corner tap Add Friends.

3.  Add a friend using any of the listed methods, or select Add by Username to input their username.

Option 3

1. While in a server, group message, or DM, you can tap on a user and then tap on the ellipsis in the top-right corner [].

2. Tap Add Friend to send a friend request. 

How to Accept or Decline a Friend Request

Desktop/Browser

1. If you have any pending friend requests, you can tap the Direct Messages icon in the top-left corner and access the Friends tab.

2. Then tap  Pending to view all of your pending friend requests. To accept a request,  tap the checkmark; to decline, tap x to decline. 

Mobile

1. Tap the Notifications tab at the bottom of the app.

2. Here you will see all pending friend requests. You can tap on Accept to approve it or Ignore to decline it.

Need help managing unwanted friend requests? Learn how to ignore users by checking out our How to Ignore Users on Discord article.

name: How to Delete your Discord Account
title: How to Delete your Discord Account
body:
If you would like to permanently delete your Discord account, this article goes over how to delete your account and what to consider before deleting your Discord account.

What this article covers:
  • How to Delete a Discord Account
    • Desktop/Browser App
    • Mobile App
  • What Happens After I Delete My Discord Account?
  • Having Trouble Deleting Your Discord Account?
  • How to Verify Your Discord Account

How to Delete a Discord Account

Discord account deletions take 15 days to process. Our Support Team is unable to speed up this process.

Desktop/Browser App

1. Go to your User Settings by pressing on the cogwheel icon in the bottom left corner of the Discord app.

Where to find the User Settings cogwheel icon on desktop/browser

2. Ensure you’ve selected the My Account tab in the left-side menu.

Example of the My Account tab under User Settings

3. At the bottom of the My Account page, select Delete Account.

Example of the Delete Account button to delete your account

4. If you haven’t done so already, you must transfer the ownership of all the servers you own or delete those servers you own. You will not be able to delete your Discord account until you have done so.

Example of the message you’ll receive if you haven’t transferred or deleted servers you own

Check out this article on how to transfer ownership of a server. Alternatively, you can learn how to delete a server here.

5. Once your ownership of your servers has been transferred, you can return to User Settings > My Account and select Delete Account once again.

6. Enter your account’s password. If you have multi-factor authentication enabled for this Discord account, you must enter the required authentication as well.

7. Press on Delete Account.

Example of the delete account window where you’ll enter your password

Mobile App

1. Tap on your profile avatar in the bottom right corner of the mobile app.

Example of where to access your profile through the mobile app

2. Tap on your profile avatar again or the gear icon in the upper right corner of the app to open Settings.

3. Tap on Account.

Account tab example which is found under User Settings

4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and press on Delete Account.

Example of where to locate the Delete Account button

5. If you haven’t done so already, you must transfer the ownership of all the servers you own. You will not be able to delete your Discord account until you have done so.

Example of the message you’ll receive if you haven’t transferred or deleted servers you own

6. Once your ownership of your servers has been transferred, you can go back to your User Settings by pressing on your profile avatar > profile avatar again or gear icon > Account and select Delete Account once again.

7. Enter your account’s password. If you have multi-factor authentication enabled for this Discord account, you must enter the required authentication as well.

8. Press on Okay.

Example of the final window to delete your account

What Happens After I Delete My Discord Account?

When you delete your Discord account, the following will occur:

  • Once you confirm that you would like to delete your account, you will be immediately logged out of your Discord account.
  • Your Discord account will be in a “pending deletion” state for 15 days from the moment you confirm that you want to delete your account.
  • Once the 15-day period ends, your Discord account will be deleted from our system and it is irreversible.
  • You will not receive notifications or friend requests.
  • You will lose access to all your servers, direct messages, group messages, and purchases.
  • Your subscriptions like Nitro and/or Server Boosts will be cancelled.
  • Any Discord server you owned under your deleted Discord account will continue to exist but with a different server owner you elect.
  • Your account will be anonymized across all servers and messages.
If you would like to cancel the deletion of your Discord account, you must restore your account within the 15-day period before your account is permanently deleted. You can learn more about how to restore your account here.

Having Trouble Deleting Your Discord Account?

If you’re having issues deleting your Discord account, here are a few things to keep in mind:

  • If you are unable to initiate the process of deleting your Discord account within the Discord app, you can reach out to our Support Team for assistance on deleting your account.
  • If you are unable to access your Discord account and you suspect that your account has been compromised so you would like to delete your account, please reach out to our Support Team.
  • If you log into your account and restore it after you initially confirmed the deletion of your account, the account deletion has been cancelled and the account will not be deleted.
  • If your account has been deleted because it was banned, disabled, or actioned on by Discord, you cannot restore it. You may submit an appeal on your account to our Trust & Safety team.
If your Discord account has been inactive and unused for 2 years or more, it will be scheduled for deletion. You may be notified of this pending deletion through the email or phone number associated with the account. You can learn more about inactive account deletions here.

How to Verify Your Discord Account

Need to verify your Discord account? Please check out these guides below.

  • How to Verify Your Discord Account: This guide will show you how to verify not only your email address, but also your phone number on your Discord account.
  • Resending Verification Email: If you need to resend your verification email, this guide will show you how.
  • How to Remove a Phone Number: If you need to remove your number in order to verify another one, this guide will show you how to do that.

name: Markdown Text 101 (Chat Formatting: Bold, Italic, Underline)
title: Markdown Text 101 (Chat Formatting: Bold, Italic, Underline)
body:
Want to inject some flavor into your everyday text chat? You're in luck! Discord uses Markdown, a simple plain text formatting system that'll help you make your sentences stand out. Here's how to do it! Just add a few characters before & after your desired text to change your text! Let’s go over some examples.

What this article covers:
  • Text Formatting
  • Organizational Text Formatting
    • Headers
    • Subtext
    • Masked Links
    • Lists
  • Code Blocks
  • Block Quotes

Text Formatting

Italics *italics* or _italics_ Underline italics __*underline italics*__
Bold **bold** Underline bold __**underline bold**__
Bold Italics ***bold italics*** underline bold italics __***underline bold italics***__
Underline __underline__ Strikethrough  ~~Strikethrough~~

Organizational Text Formatting

Headers

Note: Don’t forget to add a space between the leading heading character (#, ##, ###) and your text!

To create a header you just need to include a specific number of the hash/pound sign character (#). Use (#) for a big header, (##) for a smaller header, or (###) for an even smaller header as the first character(s) in a new line to make a header. Here is an example of what each header type looks like.

Subtext

Like Headers, you can add subtext to any chat message. To do so, add a (-# ) before the text you want to appear in the subtext. Don’t forget the space after # before your message. For example: 

Subtext works very similarly to Headers, so the (-#) must be at the very beginning of the line in order for it to work.

Masked links

You can use masked links to make text a clickable or pressable hyperlink. To do so, you need to include the text you want displayed in brackets and then the URL in parentheses. For example:

Lists

Note: Don’t forget to add a space between the list bullet (-, *, 1., etc) and your text!

You can create a bulleted list using either (-) or (*) in the beginning of each line. For example:

You can also indent your list by adding 2 spaces before (-) or (*) at the beginning of each line. For example:

Code Blocks

You can make your own code blocks by wrapping your text in backticks (`). 

If you want to create a multi-line code block, you can do so by wrapping your text in (```), like this beautifully written haiku.

Block Quotes

Note: Don’t forget to add a space between the leading > and your text!

Another option is using block quotes. To use a block quote, you just need to put (>) at the beginning of a line of text to create a single block quote. For example:


If you want to add multiple lines to a single block quote, just add (>>>) before the first line. For example:

Now you're a Discord text markdown expert. Get out there and highlight your statements! 

Note: Spoilers is another type of formatting too! Using the syntax || around your text will mark it as a spoiler. Please note, this is negated by a code block. You can learn more about Spoiler Tags here!

name: How can I change Discord's appearance/theme?
title: How can I change Discord's appearance/theme?
body:
Looking to customize Discord's appearance? Whether you need better readability or prefer the aesthetic of Dark mode, we've got several options to help you personalize your Discord experience. Learn how to change themes and customize your app's appearance.

What this article covers:
  • How to Change your Discord Theme
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • How to Change the UI Density
  • How to Change the Message Display
  • How to Use a Color for my Theme
  • How to Customize Your Theme

How to Change your Discord Theme

Desktop

First, head into your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel [], then select Appearance.

Access Theme Settings on Desktop: Open User Settings > Appearance

Discord offers several default theme options: Light, Ash, Dark, Onyx, and Sync with computer.

  • The Light theme features a white background with dark grey text and includes an optional Dark Sidebar.
  • The Ash theme uses a mid-gray background with white text. 
  • The Dark theme displays a dark gray background with white text.
  • The Onyx theme presents a gray and black background with white text.
  • Sync with computer (known as Automatic on mobile) matches your Discord theme to your device’s appearance setting.

Example of Discord Theme Selection Interface on Desktop

Mobile

Tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner of the mobile Discord app, then tap the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner. Then, scroll down and tap on Appearance.

Access Theme Settings on Mobile: Open User Settings > Appearance

At the top, you'll find these theme options: Light, Dark, Midnight, and Automatic (which syncs with your device settings).

  • The Light theme uses a white background with dark grey text. You can also enable the Dark Sidebar option.
  • The Dark theme uses a dark grey/charcoal background with white text.
  • The Midnight theme presents a gray and black background with white text.
  • Automatic matches your Discord theme to your mobile device's appearance settings.
When you enable "Sync across clients" on desktop, your theme syncs across all devices (desktop, mobile, and browser). However, themes may display slightly differently on mobile.
For instance, if you select Ash on desktop, it will appear as Dark on mobile.

Example of Discord Theme Selection Interface on Mobile

How to Change the UI Density

In the Appearance menu, scroll to UI Density. Choose between Compact, Default, or Spacious to adjust the spacing around content (and navigation spacing in the desktop app). UI density doesn’t affect message density.

UI Density options on Desktop

How to Change the Message Display

In the Appearance menu, scroll to Message Spacing > Chat Message Display.  You can choose between either Default or Compact to adjust the spacing specifically between message elements.

Chat Message Display options on Desktop

Choosing Compact will remove user icons for a denser chat view.

Example of Light Theme with Compact Message Display

Fine-tune your app's appearance using the sliders to adjust the following:

  • Zoom Level: Adjusting zoom changes the size of all Discord elements, including text. The Discord desktop app offers a slider control, while browsers use their built-in zoom function. Use Ctrl/Cmd + plus (+) to zoom in or minus (-) to zoom out.

Example of Decreasing Zoom Level

  • Chat Font Scaling: This setting adjusts only chat text size while keeping other elements unchanged. Note that the zoom level will amplify whatever font size you choose here.

Example of Increasing Chat Font Scaling

  • Message Group Spacing: Increase the space between chat messages to make conversations easier to read.

Example of Decreasing Message Group Spacing

NOTE: These steps may appear slightly different on mobile.

How to Use a Color for my Theme

Nitro subscribers can access additional themes for Discord across all platforms!

Find all available themes in User Settings under the Appearance tab on both desktop and mobile.

Nitro subscribers can customize Discord's look with colorful themes

Even without Nitro, you can preview themes on the desktop app. Select the Preview Theme button to open a preview sidebar where you can test different themes.

Preview Theme: See How Different Themes Look Before Applying

Need more help? Check our accessibility article for additional appearance settings.

How to Customize Your Theme

Custom Themes is an experimental feature available only to select Nitro subscribers on desktop.
When the “Sync across clients" toggle is enabled, custom themes applied on desktop may affect your mobile experience.
For example: On the desktop app, if you switch from dark mode to a custom theme with a light background, your mobile app will automatically switch to light mode as well. Since custom themes are not supported on mobile, the mobile app defaults to the standard light mode theme.

Make Discord match your unique vibe with custom themes! Nitro subscribers can choose custom themes with endless color combinations to customize their app’s appearance. 

1. To get started, navigate to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel icon [] located to the right of your avatar in the bottom-left corner.  

2. Press Appearance where you will find the Theme category. 

3. Under Color Themes, select the Custom Theme icon [].

Navigating to User Settings > Appearance > Theme on Desktop

4. In the Customize your theme sidebar to the right of your app, you can select the following: 

  • Select between Dark or Light mode color palettes

Selecting Between Dark and Light Mode

  • Select your custom colors using the color field and hue slider

Choosing Colors from the Color Field and Hue Slider

Tip: You can use either the color picker icon [] or enter a Hex code to select a color for your theme.

Choosing Colors Using the Color Picker or Entering a Hex Code

  • Add additional colors to your gradient by pressing Add Color 
Info: You can select up to 5 colors when creating a gradient. 

Using the Add Color Option

  • Use the Gradient Direction slider to control how your colors flow
Info: The Gradient Direction slider will only show as an option once you’ve added two or more color options.

Using the Gradient Direction Slider

  • Use the Color Intensity slider to adjust how vibrant your colors appear

Using the Color Intensity Slider

5. When you're satisfied with your changes, select Apply in the bottom-right corner of the sidebar to save them.

Apply Button in Sidebar

Tip: Press the Surprise Me icon [] in the bottom-left corner of the sidebar to generate random color combinations for your theme! 

Using the Surprise Me Icon

Tip: You can also restore your theme back to your previous custom theme by selecting the Reset button. 

Using Reset Button

name: How do I set up a Role-Exclusive announcements channel?
title: How do I set up a Role-Exclusive announcements channel?
body:
This article gives instructions for setting up an announcements channel. Some other suggested permission settings articles include creating a private server and creating a leaders channel.

If you'd like to see a general overview of how permissions work click here.

If you'd like to see how the permissions hierarchy is structured click here.

How to set up an announcements channel

1. Create a new role by clicking on the 'Roles' tab in the Server Settings menu, clicking the '+', and naming the role 'Announcements' (or whatever you want to name it).

2. Assign the 'Announcements' role to the appropriate members by clicking on the 'Members' tab in your Server Settings menu, clicking the '+' next to the appropriate members, and selecting 'Announcements' from the drop down menu.

3. Create your 'Announcements' text or channel by clicking the '+' in your channels list.

4. Name your channel 'Announcements' and click the 'Create' button.

Now you have an 'Announcements' channel!

5. Now, to limit the ability to make announcements in this channel to only members with the 'Announcements' role you need to set the channel permissions. To access the channel settings click on the cog icon next to the channel name.

6. In the Channel Settings menu click on the 'Permissions' tab.

7. Click on the @everyone role and deny the 'Send Messages' permissions by selecting the red X.

8. Click on the '+' and select the 'Announcements' role.

9. Select the 'Announcements' role to edit the channel permissions for this role. Select the green check mark to enable sending messages for this role.

Now members with the 'Announcements' role are the only people who are able to send messages in this channel. Everyone else will have read-only access to the channel.

name: Why is My Subscription Showing as Past Due?
title: Why is My Subscription Showing as Past Due?
body:
What this article covers:
  • What Does it mean when my Subscription shows as Past Due?
    • What happens to my subscription when it’s Past Due?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What Does It Mean When My Subscription Shows As Past Due?

When taking a look in your Subscriptions tab, you may notice that your Billing Information shows as past due. 

Examples of a Past Due Subscription on desktop (left) and mobile (right)

When a subscription is past due, it means that your subscription renewal payment failed. This happens when a payment fails to process on the renewal date. 

What Happens To My Subscription When It’s Past Due?

If your Nitro, Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boost subscription is past due, you will have 30 to 60 days to pay for your subscription depending on where you signed up:

  • Desktop: 30 days from the renewal date 
  • Google Play Store: 30 days from the renewal date
  • iOS App Store: 60 days from the renewal date

While your subscription is in the past due state, you will retain access to your perks for the duration of time listed above. 

If a successful payment for the subscription is not made before the window ends, the subscription will automatically end and you’ll lose access to your subscription perks and related streaks.

After you successfully make the past due payment, keep in mind that your next renewal charge may occur soon after depending on your renewal date. You can find your renewal date under Payment information in the Subscriptions Tab.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I just paid for my past due subscription? Why was I charged twice? 

A: After you have paid for your past due subscription, your next subscription renewal may be charged immediately depending on the renewal date of your subscription. You can find the date your subscription renews under User Settings > Subscriptions > Payment. 

Q: Can I cancel or change my subscription plan while it has a past due payment? 

A: You can cancel your subscription while it’s in a past due state by visiting User Settings > Subscriptions > Cancel. However, you won’t be able to change the plan you’re on until you pay for the past due payment on your current plan. Learn more about managing your subscription here. 

Q: Can I redeem my Nitro gift credits while my subscription is past due?

A: Yes, you can redeem Nitro gift credits even if your subscription is past due. If you have a Nitro gift credit before your payment fails, the credit will be applied immediately to your subscription’s upcoming billing cycle.
Also, if your account is already past due and you receive a gift credit, the credit will be applied during the next renewal attempt, and your subscription will become active again.

Note: Using a gift credit does not change the billing date for your subscription. If your account has been past due for some time (e.g., 10 days), part of the gift credit will be used to cover that period.

Q: If my payment is not made on time, what happens to my perks?

A: Depending on which platform you purchased the subscription, you’ll have access to your subscription perks for 30-60 days after your payment fails. If you do not make the payment before this window ends, your subscription will automatically end, and you will lose any perks associated with your subscription.

Q: Does my billing date change if I resolve my payment issues after my subscription is past due?

A: No. Making a payment on a subscription that’s past due does not change your renewal date.

Q: Why do I see multiple charges on my bank account?

A: The only time you should see multiple pending charges are when your payments have not been successfully processed. When renewing a subscription and your renewal payment does not successfully go through, we will attempt the purchase again to ensure that your subscription goes uninterrupted. Once a payment successfully goes through, all other pending payments are canceled.

Q: My subscription is managed by iOS or Android and my subscription went past due, what do I do?

A:  The Google Play Store allows subscriptions to be past due for a total of 30 days, while Apple (iOS) has 60 days to be past due. You will need to complete your payment through where your subscription is managed.

Q: What happens to my streaks when my subscription is past due?

A: Your streak will not be affected, as long as you make a payment during the grace period. However, if the payment is not made within the grace period then the streak will reset and can not be restored.

name: Data Used to Improve Discord
title: Data Used to Improve Discord
body:
We use certain information to help us understand and improve Discord and to develop features that make Discord safer and better for you to use. This includes information such as how you use our services, the games you play, and how servers are structured. 

Turning the Use Data to Improve Discord Setting off means we will no longer collect new information about how you use and/or navigate Discord in order to understand and improve our products. We may continue to use the information we collected when the setting was enabled. More detail can be found in our Privacy Policy. 

It will also prevent us from automatically improving the quality of voice or video communications on Discord based on your usage.

If you’d like to further assert your right to object to our processing of your data, email privacy@discord.com.

When you turn the setting off, the signals associated with your use of Discord continue to be sent, but we do not use the information for the purposes described above. This is an account-based setting and applies to your use of Discord regardless of the device used to access your account. This allows us to keep your account experience consistent across devices and access points of Discord.

name: [Known Issue] Audio Quality Drops When Joining A Call
title: [Known Issue] Audio Quality Drops When Joining A Call
body:
Listening to something on your Bluetooth headset and noticing a drop in quality when joining a Discord call? The headphones are probably switching to the Bluetooth “headset” profile. This is required for low latency and microphone functionality on most Bluetooth headphones, but it provides a lower quality audio experience. 

This is a known limitation of the Bluetooth standard that affects all apps with voice call support. The new Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy (LE Audio) standard–supported by select phones and headsets–introduces new functionality to help resolve it. Both the headset and the phone need to support LE Audio. Consult your phone and headset specifications to see if LE Audio is supported.

Support for LE Audio is coming soon to Discord, so stay tuned. 

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my headset and phone support the Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy? 

A: Consult your headset and phone specifications to see if Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy is supported. Both will need Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy support to preserve audio quality while on calls.

name: Usernames and Trademark Crossroads
title: Usernames and Trademark Crossroads
body:
We recently announced changes to how usernames and display names will work on Discord. For more information on the philosophy behind this update to usernames, you can read a message from our co-founder about why we’re changing things up now.

You may ask yourself, “What if I want to incorporate my brand's trademark into my username but it is already in use by another account?” That is a great question, and hopefully the reason you are reading this article right now, because we have an answer!

We encourage trademark holders to use a server as the home of their brand on Discord. Servers are the space where community happens on Discord. Whether that’s an organic group of friends playing games together, or customers and fans coming together to celebrate their love of an artist, brand or product, servers are where mutual experiences are shared by like-minded communities.

Discord usernames, however, are how users express themselves and choose to be known within their communities, or amongst their friends. For many Discord users, their username reflects a personal choice, not necessarily a desire to trade on the username for commercial purposes.

For these reasons, the mere use of a word or phrase in a username that might have trademark protections does not mean the username is an automatic infringement of a trademark.

Of course, Discord respects the trademark rights of others. We expect the same of our users, and take appropriate actions when presented with valid complaints. If you believe an account is in fact engaged in commerce or is trading on their username in a way which suggests they are the holder of your trademark, you can notify us by filing a report using the trademark complaint form.

If you submit a trademark complaint regarding a username, please identify specific activity carried out by the reported account indicating that the username is engaged in commerce or traded on in a misleading manner which suggests they are acting as the holder of your trademark. You can find information on how to identify specific channel ID(s) and message ID(s) in this article.

Discord will not take action on a complaint for trademark infringement regarding a username if a complaint fails to identify any of the above conduct. If you encounter a user who is impersonating an individual, group, or organization in a deceptive or harmful way, you may also report this behavior to Discord using the in-app reporting flow. Please note that you will need to report the specific message where this deceptive or harmful impersonation is taking place.

name: Troubleshooting Mobile Crashing and Installation Issues
title: Troubleshooting Mobile Crashing and Installation Issues
body:
Before trying the steps below, it’s also possible you’re using a device we do not support. To confirm please check out our requirements here.

If you’re having an issue with your Discord mobile app crashing or trouble installing the app on either iOS or Android, please try the following steps to see if this helps.

Troubleshooting Steps

1. Restart your device

The turn it off and on trick can sometimes resolve an issue, so give that a go and see if it helps.

2. Check your OS

Check to make sure your mobile device is on the latest operating system by going into your device’s settings. Be sure to download and install any software updates available.  

3. Downloading the App

Make sure you are downloading the Discord app from the Google Play Store or the Apple App Store. Currently, our mobile app is not available for download anywhere else.

4. Clear cache and Data from the App Store (Android only)

Clearing data will delete all of the app’s data. This means you will need to login to your Google account and set up your account settings again.

Sometimes clearing the cache and data can help. To start you'll want to temporarily stop the app store from running in the background by force closing the application.

Navigate to Settings > Apps > Google Play Store > on the Play Store App, tap storage > tap Clear Cache > tap Clear Data > tap Ok to confirm

5. Available phone storage

Check your available storage on your device to make sure you have enough space for the Discord app. If storage is limited, try freeing up some additional space.

6. Install over Wi-Fi or Data

Try switching between Wi-Fi and data as you could be encountering network connection issues while installing or reinstalling the app.

7. Turn off Auto Play for emojis, GIFs, and Stickers 

Navigate to Settings > Accessibility > turn off Automatically Play GIFs, animated Emojis, and Never animate for Stickers.

Still running into issues?

If nothing above resolves your issue, please reach out to Discord support at Dis.gd/contact and our support team will assist you further.

name: Voice Messages
title: Voice Messages
body:
Need to send a quick message to all of your friends but can't type because you're on the go? Or do you want to make sure your joke lands by adding comedic timing? Well, you're in luck - You can now send Voice Messages on Discord!

What this article covers:

  • What are Voice Messages?
  • How do I use Voice Messages?
    • Sending Voice Messages
    • Canceling Voice Messages
    • Listening to Voice Messages
  • How to Disable Voice Messages in your server
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Voice Messages?

Voice Messages give you the ability to send an audio recording directly to your friends. For now, you can only send Voice Messages through a direct message, group direct message, or in a server with Voice Messages enabled. These can be listened to on any device where you can access Discord, but can only be sent through the mobile app.

How do I use Voice Messages?

Sending Voice Messages

There are 2 ways to record and send a Voice Message. After navigating to the DM or server where you want to send a Voice Message, you’ll want to try one of the following:

1. Press and hold on the Mic button located on the right of the chat input box until you are done recording your message. Once completed, release the button to send the message.

2. While pressing and holding down the Mic button swipe up to lock the recording mode in place. Once you’re done recording, tap on send. 

Canceling Voice Messages

There are two ways to cancel sending a Voice Message that you recorded.

 

1. While pressing and holding the Mic button down while recording, drag your finger to the Trash icon on the left side and then release. 

2. After swiping up to lock recording mode in place, in order to cancel the recording, just tap the Trash icon on the left side.

Listening to Voice Messages

You can listen to Voice Messages on either desktop or mobile devices. To listen, simply click the “Play” button on any Voice Message for it to play. The audio will play through your default device. 

If you’re on mobile and you do not have an external audio device connected, the audio will play through your mobile speakers. 

How to Disable Voice Messages in your server

If Voice Messages are available in your server, you can disable or enable them per role. To do so, go to Server Settings > Roles and navigate to the Send Voice Messages toggle to enable or disable.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the maximum length of a Voice Message?

A: Voice Messages can be up to 20 minutes long.

Q: Can I upload my own audio files and get them to look like Voice Messages and play inline in chat?

A: No.

Q: Can I send voice messages on Discord Web or the Discord Desktop app?

A: No, you can only send voice messages from the mobile app, but you can listen to them on any Discord platform.  

Q: Can I change the audio output the Voice Message plays on?

A: On Desktop, Voice Messages will use the default audio output for Discord. On mobile, they will play through your connected device, if you do not have one connected they will play through your mobile speakers.

Q: How can I report a Voice Message?

A: To report on Desktop right click the voice message and select Report Message. To report on mobile, tap and hold on the message until you see a pop-up that says Report Message.

name: Find Your Friends FAQ
title: Find Your Friends FAQ
body:
What is Find Your Friends?

Connecting with your friends on Discord just got a whole lot easier! Introducing Find Your Friends - allowing you to discover friends on Discord using your phone contacts!

What does this article cover?

  • How does Find Your Friends work
  • How do I set up Find Your Friends
    • How do I change my name? 
    • How do I disable Find Your Friends
  • Privacy

How does Find Your Friends work:

Let’s say Wumpus and Cap are friends and Wumpus has Cap's contact in his phone.

Wumpus and Cap both are on Discord and want to find friends, so BOTH of them will need to opt-in to be discoverable via Find Your Friends.

If Wumpus enables Find Your Friends, Wumpus will then see Cap in a friend discovery list, and have the option to send him a friend request. It will look something like this:

However...

If Wumpus has Cap's contact, but Cap decides not to opt-in to be discoverable via Find Your Friends, Wumpus will not discover him.

How do I set up Find Your Friends?

1. Navigate to your Friends tab by tapping the second button to the left in the Navbar:


Filled friends list (Left), Empty friends list (right)

2. Once you are on the friends list, tap Find your friends or Getting Started. The screen will look different depending on if you already have friends on Discord or not😔. 


Filled friends list (Left), Empty friends list (right)

3. Next, you will reach the Permissions screen. Tap the toggle button to enable contacts to add you on Discord. (Tap Learn More for more details)

4. Next you will have to verify your Phone Number. If your phone number is already verified on your Discord account, you may skip this step. 

To Verify your Phone Number, enter your phone number and paste the 6 digit confirmation code (XXX-XXX)

5. Once you tap Sync Contacts with a verified phone number, a modal will show up asking for access to your contacts list.

6. Once you press Ok, we will begin syncing your contacts.

7. Once the sync is complete, we will show you the list of your contacts on Discord with Find Your Friends enabled. If none of your contacts are on Discord or have Find Your Friends Disabled, you will have the option to send them an invite. 

8. In case your contacts do not recognize you by your Discord Tag, you may change the name your contact will see when you send them an invite on this screen. 

How do I change my name?

1. To change the name that shows up in Find Your Friends, navigate to your User Settings tab by tapping the first button to the right in the Navbar (It's the button with your profile picture).

2. Once you are at your User Settings page, tap the Name setting.

3. Update your name and press Next.

How do I disable Find Your Friends?

1. To disable Find Your Friends, navigate to your User Settings tab by tapping the first button to the right in the Navbar (It's the button with your profile picture).

2. Once you are at your User Settings page, navigate to your Privacy & Safety setting.

3. Tap Allow contacts to add me to enable/disable the feature.

Note: Once disabled, your contacts will no longer discover you through the Find Your Friends feature.

Privacy

How does Discord know my contact is using Discord?

After enabling Find Your Friends, Discord periodically syncs phone numbers from your phone to Discord's servers.

These phone numbers are cryptographically hashed. When your contact also enables Find Your Friends, and if you both have agreed to be discoverable, we compare the cryptographically hashed data and detect a match. Raw phone numbers are never stored. The names visible in app are manually entered by each user so their friends can recognize them. This process allows us to prevent spam, only matches you to people you know and never to people you block. Disabling Find Your Friends or deleting your Discord account will remove all of your contact data from Discord's servers.

We won't use Find Your Friends data for any other purpose other than helping you find and invite people to Discord.

What happens after I disable Find Your Friends?

Disabling Find Your Friends or deleting your Discord account will remove all of your contact data from Discord's servers.

We won't delete any existing friend recommendations in either direction, but no new recommendations will be created.

name: Claiming a Nitro Gift FAQ
title: Claiming a Nitro Gift FAQ
body:
Important Notes:
- Before claiming a gift, make sure you are logged into the correct Discord account on the desktop/browser version of the app!
- If you accidentally claimed the gift on the wrong account, Discord is unable to provide you with another code or transfer the gift!

What this article covers:

  • Claiming a Gift sent within Discord
  • Claiming a Gift sent outside of Discord
  • Already Claimed Gifts
  • What if I already have an Active Nitro Subscription?
    • How do I activate my Account Credit?

Claiming a Gift sent within Discord

If you're already logged into your account on the browser or desktop version of the Discord app, you can easily claim a gift!

1. If you're in a DM or server in Discord and you've received a gift link, you can directly press on the Open gift button that's tied to the gift! 

2. You'll see a confirmation pop-up asking you to accept the gift! Press the  Accept gift button in this confirmation window to apply the gift to your Discord account! 

3. After accepting the gift to your account, you'll then see a confirmation that the subscription has been directly applied to your Discord account!

Claiming a Gift sent outside of Discord

If you receive a code within your email or through another platform, you can follow these steps below to claim your gift to your Discord account!

Step 1 - Clicking the Gift Link

  • Start by directly clicking the gift link or copying and pasting the gift link into your browser window.

Step 2 - Logging into Discord

  •  If you're not logged into Discord already in your browser, you will then be automatically redirected to either:

Register for a New Account

If you don't have an account, you can directly register a new Discord account

Login to your Account

If you already have a Discord account, you can login to your account using your email and password or using QR code login

Step 3 - Confirming the Correct Account

  • Once you have logged into your Discord account, you'll see a new message asking you to confirm if you would like to accept the gift. Be sure to double-check that you’re logged into the correct Discord account. When you're ready to claim this gift, press the I accept button. 

Step 4 - Gift Now Activated

  • After accepting the gift to your account, you'll now be automatically redirected to your Subscriptions tab in your User Settings to see your newly activated gift subscription on your account.

Already Claimed Gifts

If you're not sure when a gift has been claimed or not, you can double check by clicking and opening the link in your browser! If a gift has been successfully claimed, you'll see a "This gift has already been claimed" error in the browser. 

If you're already using the browser or desktop version of Discord, and you're viewing a gift link shared within Discord, you'll see there is a grayed out "Claimed" button in the gift after it has been claimed!

What if I already have an Active Nitro Subscription?

Whenever you accept a gift while you have a running subscription, or accept a gift that differs from your current subscription, that gifted subscription will be added to your Discord account as Account Credit. 

To view your Account Credit:

  1. Start by logging into your Discord account on the desktop or browser version of the app
  2. Head into your User Settings (by clicking on the cog icon in the bottom left corner)
  3. Then select the Subscriptions tab in the left side bar

Note:
Account Credit can only be used for desktop/browser subscriptions. It cannot be used on Google Play or iOS App Store subscriptions. 

How do I activate my Account Credit?

When your current Nitro subscription has expired or is removed, the Account Credit for the gift will apply when you activate that matching subscription on the desktop/browser Discord app! 

For example, if you currently have 9.99 Nitro Monthly Credit, you will need to activate a 9.99 Nitro Monthly subscription to use this account credit!

Note: 
- The account credit will only be consumed for redeeming exact matching subscription plans in both type and time! (Nitro > Nitro, Nitro Basic > Nitro Basic, Monthly > Monthly, Yearly > Yearly)
- If the subscriptions do not match, the account credit will not be applied!

To activate the matching subscription:

    1. Start by heading to the Subscription tab, you'll need to press the Subscribe button for the matching subscription type for Discord Nitro or Nitro Basic. 
    2. Then a new window will pop up where you will need to select the matching plan for the subscription. 
    3. If your Discord account does not have your payment information, you'll be asked to fill out your payment details. (Note: You will not be charged unless the subscription renews)
    4. Once you've finished submitting that information, you'll then see a "Subscription Credit applied" message as you are reviewing the purchase details for activating the subscription
    5. After you confirm your activation, your gifted subscription will then be activated! 

Have any other questions? 

If you have any questions around claiming gifts or account credit, just contact our support team at dis.gd/billing and we'll be able to look into your question further from there!

name: Google Play Store Integration FAQ
title: Google Play Store Integration FAQ
body:
What this article covers:

  • How do I Purchase A Subscription on Android?
  • How do I Change my Subscription?
  • How do I Cancel my Subscription?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How do I Purchase A Subscription on Android?

1. Start by heading into your User Settings by tapping on your avatar in the bottom right corner.

2. You'll then need to scroll down until you see the Nitro Settings section! From here, tap on Subscribe Today to start the process.

3. You'll then see the option to purchase Nitro or Nitro Basic.

4. You'll then be asked to confirm if you want Yearly or Monthly, then you can tap on purchase to proceed.

 

5. You'll then see a Google Play menu pop up explaining your subscription purchase pricing and asking what payment method you want to use.

6. Once you've confirmed your subscription with the Subscribe button (and scanning your fingerprint or inputting your password [if applicable] to verify your purchase), you'll then see a confirmation that your Nitro has been activated.

How do I Change my Subscription?

If you ever change your mind on the type of subscription you have, you can always switch your subscription as well.

1. To start, head into your User Settings, scroll down until you see the Nitro Settings section once more, and then select the Manage Subscriptions tab.

2. In this tab, tap the Switch Plans button (right beside the Manage Boosts button), and you'll be given the option to choose from all the other subscription types.

 

3. Once you have made a decision on what kind of subscription you'd like, you will see the Google Play menu pop up explaining your subscription change, and reviewing the new subscription pricing. 

4. When you're ready to make the purchase, tap Subscribe, and you'll see a confirmation that your subscription was activated. 

5. When you head back into your Manage Subscription tab, you'll then see a notification that your plan change is pending. And soon, your tab will update to show your new subscription.

How do I Cancel my Subscription?

1. Head into your User Settings and scroll down once more to your Nitro settings section to head into your Manage Subscriptions tab. Then tap on the Cancel button.

2. You'll then be redirected to the Google Play Store app, where you'll need to confirm your decision by tapping on Cancel Subscription. 

3. Once the cancellation is confirmed, and you go back to your Discord mobile app, you'll see the canceled subscription in your Manage Subscription tab.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What does creating a subscription through Google Play get me?

A: Creating a subscription through Google Play will allow you to use Google Pay as a payment option for your subscription or would like to manage your subscription in the Google Play store along other subscriptions.

Q: I don't see the type of plan that I want to purchase, does that mean I can't purchase that?

A: At launch, we've had to limit the number of plans available for purchase on Android. If you don't see the plan type that you want to purchase you can still go on the desktop or browser app and purchase that plan through that platform. You will still be able to use the benefits on your Android device if you purchase through desktop.

Q: I already bought a subscription that I use on Android. Does this change anything about that?

A: If you're happy with your current subscription, you don't need to change anything! However, moving forward any changes you want to make to that subscription will need to be done through the desktop/browser app.

Q: I currently have a subscription on desktop, but want to move it to manage it through the Google Play store. How do I do that?

A: You can cancel your subscription on desktop and then re-subscribe through the Android app. However, make sure that you wait until the end of your current billing period to sign back up on Android. 

Please note if you cancel your subscription on Android you will either have to sign up for Google Play or sign back up on desktop, but manage your subscription through desktop only. If you cancel your desktop subscription and re-sign up on desktop later you will also lose your streak. The only way to maintain your streak is to continue with your desktop subscription or sign up to Google Play within 7 days of the original desktop subscription ending.

Q: Will I lose my streak if I switch my subscription over to Google Play?

A: If you re-subscribe within 7 days after your desktop subscription ends to a subscription within Google Play your Nitro streak will transfer over and not be lost.

Q: Why can't I do certain gifting actions through Google Play?

A: Currently, you can purchase and send gifts through Google Play. If you have a desktop subscription you will be able to redeem, apply, and send gifts through your Android app.

Note:
- Currently, gifts purchased through Google Play cannot contribute towards subscriptions managed by the Google Play Store.
- Redeemed gifts can still contribute towards subscriptions purchased on our desktop or browser apps.

If you're on the Android app, and you already have a Google Play subscription and you redeem a gift purchased through the Google Play store, your redeemed Nitro gift will not contribute towards that subscription and it will become Account Credit that can be used for a subscription on our desktop or browser app!

If you're on the Android app, and you have no active subscription when you redeem a gift purchased through the Google Play store, you will begin a subscription that can be managed on the desktop or browser app! 

Q: Why can't I create a subscription through Google Play when I already created one on my Android device?

A: You can only have one active platform subscription at a time. If you previously created a subscription on your Android device you currently have a desktop subscription that will need to be managed through your desktop or browser app.

Q: If I currently have a subscription through iOS can I manage that subscription on my Android phone?

A: If you currently have a subscription through iOS you will not be able to purchase, cancel, or otherwise manage your subscription on an Android device.

Q: What happens when I upgrade or downgrade a subscription in Google Play?

A: Similar to a desktop subscription your upgrade will be immediate and the price will be pro-rated. Downgrades will occur at the next billing cycle.

Q: I tried to upgrade my subscription and add onto my current subscription, but it got swapped to another subscription instead! Why did my subscription get swapped instead of upgraded? 

A: Please note that subscription plans on Google Play cannot be added to each other and you will only be able to switch between plans.

If you wish to upgrade your subscription, you will need to switch to the plan that includes all of the subscriptions you wish to purchase.

For example:

If you currently have a Nitro Basic subscription, and you would like to update your subscription to include 2 Server Boost subscriptions as well, you will then need to manually select the "Nitro Basic + 2 Server Boost" subscription plan.

If you currently have a Nitro Basic subscription, and you select to purchase the "2 Server Boost" subscription plan, your Nitro Basic subscription will be removed, and you will only have an active subscription for 2 Server Boosts.

name: Getting Started on Mobile
title: Getting Started on Mobile
body:
If you are new to Discord and would like to create an account via your mobile device, this guide will help walk you through the steps.

What this article covers:

  • Creating an Account
  • Setting up an Account
    • Changing Your Avatar
    • Changing Your Account Details
  • Adding Friends
    • Sending Friend Requests 
    • Adding a Friend in a Server
    • Accepting Friend Requests
  • Joining Servers
  • Creating DMs and Group Chats
  • How to Start a Voice Call
  • How to Answer a Voice Call
  • How to Use Speaker Phone while in a Voice Call
  • Expressing Yourself
    • Sending Photos and Files
    • Sending Gifs
    • Adding Emojis
    • Adding Reactions

Creating an Account

1. If you’d like to create a Discord account and start using the app, you can download Discord via your mobile device: 

  • For Android devices, head into the Play Store 
  • For iOS, head into the App Store 

2. Once the app is fully installed, tap on the app icon to launch the app. 

3. If this is your first time using Discord, press Register to create your account. You’ll need to enter:

  • a display name
  • a username
  • your email address or phone number
  • a password

4. Once you’ve finished entering this account information, you can then select Next to start using Discord. 

Remember to head into your email to verify your email address. By verifying your email address, you’ll be able to recover your account if you ever forget your password.

If your new account is not verified, your username will be given a random 5 digits to the end of your username after 7 days from account creation.

     

Setting up an Account

1. To set up your account, tap on your profile icon in the bottom right hand corner. 

2. Then, tap the cogwheel [] in the upper right corner. 

3. This will take you to your Settings where you can select various options to personalize your account.

     

Changing Your Avatar

1. If you’d like to change your avatar, tap your profile icon to navigate to your Profile. 

2. Then, tap on Edit Profile and select your profile icon to change your profile picture.

3. After you’ve selected your desired photo, you can adjust the image by zooming in or out of the photo. Then, select the Choose option in the bottom right to reflect the changes. 

4. The image preview will now be reflected in your profile. If it’s to your liking, pressing Save in the upper right corner will save your changes.

Along with customizing your avatar, Nitro members can also add an animated avatar. If you’d like to learn more about animated avatars, you can check out this article.  

Changing Your Account Details

As you continue exploring Discord, you may wish to change your username or even your email address associated with your account. 

1. If you would like to change your account details, head over to your Settings and tap Account. 

2. Once redirected to Account, you will see that you can select various options. To edit a specific account detail, tap the specific option. 

3. Before the changes are solidified, you will be asked to verify your password to confirm the changes. Then, you should be all set!  

   

4. Additionally, if you ever need to change your password, you’ll be able to press Password in the Account settings.

You can only change your username and avatar two times in an hour! So if you’ve reached the limit for the hour, you’ll need to wait before changing your name again! 

Adding Friends

Now that you’ve officially created an account, you can directly add friends or receive friend requests from people that you already know on Discord!

Sending Friend Requests  

1. To send a friend request, be sure to tap the Messages tab in the bottom row. 

2. Once you have been redirected to Messages, tap the Add Friends button in the upper right corner.

3. To add your friend by their username, tap @ Add by Username and input your friend’s username.

4. Once you’ve typed in your friend’s Discord username and press Send Friend Request, a request will be directly sent!

If you're not able to send a request, it's possible that your friend needs to change their Privacy and Safety Settings for who can add them as a Friend. Check out the Friend Request section in our article on Privacy Settings for more details. 

If you’d like to view your previously added friends, you can tap on your profile icon in the bottom right corner and select Your Friends.

   

Make sure that you’re typing your friend’s username exactly as spelled and double check capitalization since usernames are case sensitive. Additionally, make sure to remove any extra spaces.

Adding a Friend in a Server

1. If you’re already in a server, and you’d like to add someone you’ve become friends with, you can tap on the channel’s name located at the very top to navigate to the Members list and tap on the person’s username to view their profile. You can also  tap the user’s avatar in a message to view their profile. 

2. While there, you’ll be able to select the Add Friend option to send a Friend Request. 

Accepting Friend Requests

If you’ve received a Friend Request, you’ll see a red notification on your Notifications tab. 

1. Press the bell icon located in the bottom row to be redirected to the Notifications tab.

2. Then, you can check your pending friend requests by tapping on the Friend Requests icon in the upper right corner. 

3. Once you’ve been redirected to the Friend Request tab, you can view and choose to accept or decline pending requests. 

   

To check if you are adding the correct friend, tap on the requester’s icon to view the requester’s User Profile.  

Joining Servers

You can either press directly on an invite link from your friend to automatically join the server, or you can manually enter an invite link through the Join Server menu.

Joining a Server Directly  Manually Entering a Server Invite Link

1. To manually enter an invite link that you’ve received, start by tapping the green plus sign button in the left side bar. 

2. You’ll then see the option to create or join a server. Select the Join a Server button and then manually input the invite link or the last string of the link that you’ve received. 

3. Once you fill out the appropriate invite link, you can tap the Join Server button.  

4. Afterwards, you will need to accept the invitation to confirm that you’re joining the correct server.

Creating DMs and Group Chats

If you’d like to have a smaller group chat outside of the server you can create a group chat. 

1. To start, tap Messages in the bottom row and select the New Message icon.

2. Then, you’ll be able to select New Group and select your friends you’d like to add into the group chat.

   

You can select up to 10 friends to join within a group direct message. 

3. Once you’ve selected the friends you’d like to add, tap Create in the upper right corner. This will redirect you to the new group message you have just created.

 

How to Start a Voice Call

1. In order to call a friend and start a voice call with them, you first want to tap the Chat Bubble [] in the top left corner of the Discord mobile app.

2. Tap on your friend’s avatar icon at the top of the Direct Message list or in the DM you share with them. 

3. Tap on Phone Call icon [] at the top-right of the DM to start a Voice Call.

4. To end the call, tap on the End Call icon [] in the bottom-right corner when in the Voice Call screen.

How to Answer a Voice Call

1. If a friend is calling you and you want to answer, you can tap on the check mark or on the Phone Call icon [].

2. To end the call, tap on the End Call icon [] in the bottom-right corner when in the Voice Call screen.

How to use Speaker Phone while in a Voice Call

There are 2 ways to enable speaker phone while in a voice call: 

Option 1

1. Tap on the speaker icon [] in the top-right corner while in a call to enable speaker mode.

Option 2

1. While in a call, swipe up from the bottom screen to display all available call audio options. Tap on Change Audio Output.

2. Tap on Speaker to enable speaker phone.

Expressing Yourself

Now that you’re connected with your friends in servers and DMs, you can now start chatting away through text, emojis, photos and more! 

Sending Photos and Files

Want to stay in chat and directly send a photo without opening your camera app? 

1. You can send a photo on the fly to your friends by tapping the Add File () icon in the bottom left corner. 

2. This will let you view your photos within your photo gallery or select the Camera button.

3. If you would like to directly take a photo, select the Camera button to open the Camera app within Discord. Then, you will be able to take a photo. 

4. Once you have taken or chosen the photo, you will be able to send a message along with the photo to your friends.

Sending Gifs

You’ll also be able to send gifs directly into chat by using the GIF Picker! 

1. To send a gif, tap the emoji icon located to the right of the message bar. This icon resembles a smiley face. 

2. Once you have tapped the emoji icon, the Emoji, GIFs, and Stickers selection menu will appear. 

3. Select the GIFs tab to view and choose various gifs to send to your friends. If you’d like to search for a specific gif, you can type within the Search Tenor bar to populate more choices. 

Adding Emojis

You can directly send emojis through chat by pressing on that Emoji icon in the message bar! 

You’ll be able to see your most frequently used emojis, or directly search for the exact emoji you’re looking for in the emoji search bar! 

Adding Reactions

Not only are you able to send emojis within messages, but you can also choose an emoji to react to posted messages. 

1. To add a reaction on the mobile app, long press the message you’d like to react to. This will allow a new menu to appear. 

2. From this menu, you can choose one of your frequently used emojis as a reaction, or you can directly search for a specific emoji to use as a reaction by pressing on the Reactions icon.  

3. If another person has already reacted to the message, you can tap on their reaction to add to the reaction counter or you press on the emoji icon to select another emoji you’d like to add. 

     

Nitro members can also add Super Reactions to add a little more hype, emotion, and intensity to your reaction! You can learn more about Super Reactions here. 

And you've made it! 

Hopefully this guide helped you to understand the basics of getting started on Discord mobile! For other useful guides to learn more about Discord, check out these articles below.

  • Getting Started
  • Beginner's Guide to Discord
  • Discord Voice and Video Troubleshooting Guide

If you run into any issues or have any questions, feel free to contact our support team here.

name: Go Live and Screen Share
title: Go Live and Screen Share
body:
Want to learn more?
This article covers How to Screen Share and Go Live on Discord in DMs and voice channels on the desktop client. For more information on how to start a video call check out our Video Calls article. If you have questions about screen sharing on a mobile device, please review our [Mobile] Screenshare FAQ article.
What this article covers:
  • What is Go Live and Screen Share? 
    • How to Stream in a Discord Channel
  • How do I Screen Share my Game on Discord? 
    • Screen Share Your Game Using Overlay
    • How do I screen share in a Direct Message?
  • Stream Quality Settings
    • Stream Quality Settings for Go Live
    • Screen Share Stream Quality Settings For Direct Messages  
      • View Modes
      • Window Modes
      • Audio Sharing
  • Go Live: Screen Share Server Permissions
  • How to Enable or Disable Screen Share Stream Preview
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • How do I watch a Stream?
    • Troubleshooting for a Go Live Viewer
    • Go Live: Pop Out

What is Go Live and Screen Share?

Go Live and Screen Share allows you to screen share any application window, or your entire screen in a Discord server or voice call. Up to 50 people can share their video or screen at a time in a Discord voice chat.

How to Stream in a Discord Channel

Here is how to Screen Share and Go Live in a Discord server:

1. Join a voice channel in your server that you have permissions to screen share in.

2. Tap on the Screen streaming icon in the voice status panel (near the bottom left corner) and a new window will pop out.

3. Select an individual application window to share, or select an entire screen to share.

4. Tap the "Go Live" button at the bottom of the window when you are ready to share your stream. 

How to stream in a Discord voice channel

Info: Currently audio can only be captured by the Windows desktop, MacOS desktop, Chrome browser, and mobile clients. Unfortunately, audio sharing is unavailable on Linux.

How do I Screen Share my Game on Discord?

To share your game it needs to be recognized by our built-in game detection system. 

Tip: If the game does not appear, try manually adding your game by going to User Settings > Game Activity > Add it.
Info: Unfortunately, if your game is not recognized by Game Detection, or through the process of manually adding it, then you will not be able to stream the game.

Option 1

1. Join a voice channel in your server that you have permissions to screen share in.

2. Tap on the Screen streaming icon in the voice status panel (near the bottom left corner) and a new window will pop out.

3. Select the individual app for the game that you want to stream.

4. Tap the "Go Live" button at the bottom of the window when you are ready to share your stream. 

Screen sharing a game through Discord

Option 2

1. While in a Voice Channel with the game you want to stream open tap on the Stream icon to stream your game

Stream icon

2. Here you can pick the Voice Channel you want to stream to (if you’re not already in one), and change any of the stream settings (quality and framerate) and tap on Go Live to stream.

Pick the voice channel you want to stream in

You should see a small Picture-in-Picture (PiP) window of the game you're sharing so you can view how it looks. Hovering over the PiP will give you options to adjust the stream’s settings or end the stream.

Picture-in-Picture (PiP) window

Tip: The PiP window will be automatically paused once you have the game in focus.

Screen Share Your Game Using Overlay

You can also share your game through the Discord overlay.

1. While your game is open, toggle your Discord overlay by tapping on the hot key (shift+` for default).

2. Then tap on Stream and choose what settings you’d like to use

3. Finally, tap on Go Live to start the stream

Screen sharing through the Discord overlay

If someone is watching your stream, you’ll see a little eyeball icon 👁 next to their name in the overlay.

Eyeball icon

How do I screen share in a Direct Message?

To share your screen in a Direct Message (DM), you'll want to start a call first. You can do this by tapping the phone or video icon in the top header while viewing a DM.

Screen share through a direct message

1. Tap on the Share Your Screen icon to start streaming in a DM.

2. Next, pick either the Application you want to stream or what Screen you’d like to share. To pick, tap on what you’d like to share.

3. Finally, you can pick what settings you’d like to stream with. Tap on Go Live when you’re ready to stream.

Screen sharing through a direct message

Tip: Tip: If you want to swap from one app window to another, you’ll be able to easily swap by selecting the "Change Window" option!

Stream Quality Settings

Info:
- All users can stream up to 720p/30fps.
- Nitro Classic subscribers have access to 1080p/60fps.
- And Nitro subscribers can go all the way up to 4k/60fps.

The frame rate and resolution of your stream can be adjusted from multiple different places.

Regardless if you're sharing your screen in a Direct Message or a server voice channel, you can always change your Stream Quality by selecting the "Screen" button above your status bar. 

Stream quality settings

Tip: When streaming through browser, you can not adjust the stream’s quality.

Stream Quality Settings For Go Live

While streaming, you can adjust the stream quality at any time. 

1. While sharing your screen in a server’s voice channel hover over your PiP and tap on the gear icon

2. Next, select Stream Quality

3. Here you can change the Frame Rate and Resolution.

How to change stream quality settings while live

Screen Share Stream Quality Settings For Direct Messages

Here is how to edit your stream quality while streaming through a Direct Message.

1. While streaming in a Direct Message tap on the down arrow. 

2. Next, tap on Stream Quality.

3. Now you can adjust your Frame Rate and Resolution. 

Screen share quality settings while in a direct message

View Modes

Grid View 

All calls will automatically start in this view. This is the perfect view to see all the videos/screenshares within your chat at once.

Grid view

Focus View
