Now with tabs and some improvements to the friends page, it will only take 3. And it can have its own notification badges so you won’t miss a new request.

  • Quick Switcher and Recent Mentions: To our users who are a part of many communities, we built the Quick Switcher and Recent Mentions features to make it easier to navigate around and find messages relevant to you. When we rolled out experiments with giving these features their own space, we noticed that the use of the Quick Switcher nearly doubled! We’ll be making improvements to these experiences as well -- stay tuned!

  • User Settings: Your own user settings can be accessed on the right-most tab that displays your avatar and status. Power-user of custom statuses? No problem -- you can still change them directly from the tabs view by long-pressing the User Settings tab.

While we’re excited about the power of tabs, we also wanted to keep the app uncluttered, especially while you're in a conversation. So we decided that you should only see the tabs when you need them. The tabs will slide them away when you’re viewing a channel or DM.

The Future

Finally, tabs give us the flexibility to keep investing in making Discord more useful to our users. As an example, millions of users on the desktop have used server discovery to find communities relevant to their interests. In a post-tabs world, we now have a few options to bring a better way to discover new servers to mobile without cluttering the app. 

As always, we’re constantly looking for ways to improve. Let us know if you have any feedback!

name: Changing Your DNS Provider
title: Changing Your DNS Provider
body:
Ever had trouble connecting to Discord or seeing content in your favorite chats? One of the most common issues coming between you and your friends' cat pics is your domain name service provider. The domain name service, or DNS provider, is the service your computer uses to translate the text and code delivered by webpages into sweet and tasty internet content goodness.

Why Change DNS Providers?

Swapping your provider can make for a faster and more reliable web experience, and can often even improve your privacy, too! Changing your DNS provider is also one of the first solutions we recommend if you're encountering one of the following common service issues:

  • Degraded voice quality
  • Images not loading
  • Stuck in an update loop
  • Unable to download Discord
  • Can't connect to voice chat

Which Should I Use?

Here at Discord, we typically recommend Google Public DNS and Cloudflare 1.1.1.1. Both Google and Cloudflare are trusted and dependable service providers whose servers we rely on for hosting Discord! We recommend these options because they deliver the most consistent and speedy access to text chat, images, videos, and even voice chat!

Google Public DNS is easy to use on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It can even work on your mobile device's wifi connection if you're willing to mess with some device settings!

Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 works on computers just as well as Google Public DNS, but for users on mobile devices running Android and iOS, they offer a mobile app that lets you use their service as a replacement DNS provider for while you're on cellular data and not just wifi!

The steps for changing your provider look different based on your platform, and the IP addresses can change over time, so we always recommend checking out the websites linked above first. That said, you can find some simple walkthroughs for various platforms below!

Windows 7 and 10

  1. Open the Start menu, then type to search for and open the Control Panel
  2. Select Network and Internet, then select Network and Sharing Center
  3. Select Change adapter settings, then right click the connection you're currently using and select Properties
  4. Select Internet Protocol Version 4 and enter the IPv4 addresses listed by Google or Cloudflare.
  5. Select Internet Protocol Version 6 and enter the IPv6 addresses listed by Google or Cloudflare.
  6. Click OK, then OK to close the Properties screen, then restart your browser and you're good to go!

macOS

  1. Open System Preferences in the Apple menu
  2. Select Network, then select the connection you're currently using and click Advanced...
  3. Open the DNS tab, then remove any servers listed currently.
  4. Press the + icon to add your new IPv4 and IPv6 DNS addresses, as listed by Google or Cloudflare.

iOS and Android

  1. We typically recommend downloading the Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 app from the Apple App Store or the Google Play Store for ease of use!
  2. Advanced users can find instructions on how to manually change their WiFi DNS addresses on the Google Public DNS website for Android and iOS.

Note: When using Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 on your mobile device, you do not have to use Cloudflare's Warp or Warp+ VPN service in order to take advantage of their free DNS option!

Now you're all ready to browse the web with better speed--and hopefully, some of your most common Discord troubles should be resolved, too! If you're still running into a specific connection issue even after swapping your DNS provider, our support team is here to help you 24/7, too.

name: Spellcheck in Discord
title: Spellcheck in Discord
body:
Discord's spellchecker is available on machines currently running macOS and Windows 10+.

Doo youe ned a litle halp wiht wat yur typeing in Diskord? Well, we have you covered. If enabled, you can use your system’s spell checker to check for possible typos!

What this article covers: 

  • How to add words to Spellcheck
  • How to disable Spellcheck
  • How to set your language
    • Windows
    • macOS

How to add a words to Spellcheck

Did you accidentally add a word to Spellcheck? Since the spellchecker is based on the dictionary in your computer’s system, you’ll need to go into your computer’s settings to remove the word.

If a word is getting flagged by the Spellcheck, you can add the word to your dictionary.

1. To do this, after the squiggle appears under the word indicating the spelling needs to be checked, right-click and tap on Add to Dictionary.

2. Now the word is in your dictionary! 

How to disable Spellcheck

While using the desktop app, if at any point you want to turn off the Spellcheck, all you have to do is right-click on a chat window and uncheck the Spellcheck box.

To enable it again, simply follow the same steps above and make sure the box next to Spellcheck has a check mark.

How to set your language

Spellcheck is based on the language of your system and Discord. If your system is a different language than your Discord app, it may flag words that are spelled correctly. Here are some steps on how to set your language on your device.

Windows

1. Open up Language settings on your system.

2. You’ll see an option to not only set your Windows display language, but any additional preferred languages.

3. After adding additional preferred languages you’ll be prompted to install a language pack for each one. Once completed, you can change your Windows display language.

macOS

1. Go to your Keyboard settings then Text Input.

2. Here you can set your language preference and add any additional languages by tapping on the plus (+).

3. After you finish adding any additional languages, you can tap on Done.

name: Deceased or Incapacitated Users
title: Deceased or Incapacitated Users
body:
What this article covers:

  • Submitting Requests Regarding Deceased or Incapacitated Users on Discord
    • Requesting Access or Details for the Deceased’s Account
    • Requesting Account Deletion
  • Billing or Payment-Related issues
  • Requests to Memorialize or Transfer an Account
  • Inactive Account Deletion
  • Contacting Discord Support
  • Further Information

Submitting Requests Regarding Deceased or Incapacitated Users on Discord

At Discord, we understand that dealing with the accounts of deceased or incapacitated users can be a sensitive and challenging situation. We are here to guide you through the process of submitting requests regarding their Discord account while ensuring privacy and security for all parties involved. 

Requesting Access or Details for the Deceased’s Account

Due to privacy and security reasons, we are unable to provide access, disclose personal information, make changes, or share data tied to an account. However, if you have access to the email address associated with the account, you can initiate a password reset. This process allows you to regain access to the account without compromising privacy and security. To learn more about how to reset a password, please refer to this support article.

Requesting Account Deletion

If you have access to the deceased user’s Discord account you can follow the steps below to initiate the account deletion process:

1. Log into the deceased user's Discord account on the mobile or desktop application or discordapp.com.

2. Enter the User Settings by clicking on the cog icon on the bottom left of your Discord app.

3. Once you’re in the My Account tab (it should be the default tab), scroll down to the section titled Account Removal.

4. Click on the Delete Account button, and you’ll be prompted to enter the password for this Discord account.

5. After you have confirmed the deletion, you will be immediately logged out of the account and the deletion process will begin.

For more information about account deletion, check out our Support article: https://support.discordapp.com/hc/en-us/articles/212500837.

If you have access to the deceased user’s email address or if you are writing in from the email associated with the account:

You can request account deletion by including the following sentence in your request:
"I confirm that I would like to delete the account associated with [emailaddress@email.com]." while replacing the email address with the email address in question. Once we receive the request above, we will be able to begin the account deletion process. 

If you are requesting account deletion from a different account or email address:

Since Discord prioritizes user privacy and does not collect extensive personal information on our users, verifying the identity and relationship of the requester is crucial. In order to proceed with account-related actions, the following documentation must be provided:

  • Deceased User's Account Details:
    • Email address associated with the account
    • Discord Username
  • Proof of Account Holder's Death:
    • Death certificate or coroner's report
  • Proof of Your Relationship to the Deceased:
    • Marriage license, birth certificate, last will and testament, estate letter, or power of attorney
  • Verification of Your/the Requestor’s Identity:
    • Valid photo ID or passport

Document Submission Guidelines:

Please ensure that the documents are provided as photocopies or scanned copies. To safeguard your privacy, you can block out any personal information such as birthdays and addresses while keeping names visible.

Explicit Confirmation of Action Requested:

In addition to the required documents, we need an explicit confirmation of the action you are requesting for the account. Please include the following statement: "I request to have the account associated with [email and/or username] deleted."

Billing or Payment-Related issues

If you have any questions regarding billing or payments related to a deceased user’s account, please visit our support form, select Billing, and choose the type of billing issue that most closely relates to your question.

Requests to Memorialize or Transfer an Account

We do not currently have a feature to memorialize or transfer accounts. However, you can submit the feature as a request to our feedback site found at https://feedback.discord.com. 

Inactive Account Deletion

Discord accounts that have not been used for 2 years or more may be scheduled to be deleted due to inactivity. As the Deceased’s account nears the 2 years mark, their email address or phone number may get an email or text message with a warning that their account is scheduled to be deleted. As long as no one logs into the account in question, the deletion will proceed automatically. 

Contacting Discord Support

1. Initial Contact:

  • Please send a support request to Discord Support and provide the necessary information and documents as outlined above.

  • Wait for a response from our support team.

2. Response and Follow-up:

  • You might receive a response from our support team requesting additional information or clarification.

  • If you are able to provide further information, rest assured that we will use it exclusively for the purpose of addressing your request.

3. Privacy and Security:

  • Discord takes user privacy and security seriously. Personal information, documents, and correspondence will be handled confidentially and used solely for verification and processing purposes.

Further Information

For more information about our approach to privacy and data security, please review our Privacy Policy.

name: EU DSA Dispute Resolution Options
title: EU DSA Dispute Resolution Options
body:
This article explains how users covered by the European Union’s Digital Services Act (“DSA”) can exercise certain rights. Parts of the DSA only apply to certain online spaces (called “online platforms”) and to certain types of actions by those platforms. That’s all to say that not every report or action on Discord will be eligible for action under the DSA. 

We work hard to remove violative content and bad actors from our services. This includes responding to user reports about content. The easiest way to report content that violates our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines is through our in-app reporting surfaces.  Certain users also have the option to report illegal content under the DSA through this webform. 

The DSA also provides specific appeal rights for certain users. If the DSA applies to you and you think we’ve made a mistake in arriving at one of the decisions listed below, you have six months to appeal our decision through our internal appeals process.  A link to appeal Discord’s decision can be found on the violation notice.

You may also appeal a decision on your account directly in the Discord app by going to User Settings > Privacy & Safety > selecting the decision you want to appeal > Let us know.

 

Please keep in mind that these DSA appeals mechanisms only apply to decisions about the following, if they are made on the ground that information provided is illegal or violates our Terms of Service: 

  • removing or disabling access to or restricting visibility of content; 
  • suspending or terminating access to Discord (in whole or in part); 
  • suspending or terminating a user’s Discord account; or 
  • suspending, terminating, or restricting a user’s ability to monetize their Discord activity.

You may also have the option of selecting an out-of-court dispute settlement body certified by an EU Member State’s Digital Services Coordinator to help resolve a dispute relating to any such decision.  The European Commission will maintain a website listing the available settlement bodies as they become certified. Discord will work with the out-of-court settlement body where required by law, but is not bound by any decisions made by these out-of-court settlement bodies. Discord also has the right not to engage with an out-of-court dispute settlement body if a dispute has already been resolved concerning the same information and the same grounds.

name: Community Guidelines Updates
title: Community Guidelines Updates
body:
Our Community Guidelines are the foundation for how we work to keep you safe and ensure that Discord stays the best place to talk, hang out, and have fun with friends online.

One of our main goals with today’s update to the Community Guidelines was to make our rules easier to understand. After each guideline, we’ve added a link to our Policy Hub, where we explain our policies in greater detail.

Below is a quick summary of two other important changes — but, please do read the full guidelines, as they actually govern your use of Discord. The changes go into effect on April 15, 2024.

  • We’ve separated our doxxing and harassment guidelines. Previously, doxxing was combined with our harassment guideline. However, we consider these distinct harm types, so we separated them to better reflect how we organize our policies.
  • We’ve created a new, “Follow the Law” section. In last year’s version of the Community Guidelines, we referenced multiple types of illegal behavior in a single guideline. Now, we’ve expanded that guideline into its own section, which allows us to more clearly explain how we assess dangerous and illegal behaviors.

name: Stage Channel Guidelines
title: Stage Channel Guidelines
body:
Stages are a new way to connect you and your community to the things that everyone is passionate about in a more personal way — whether it be a specific video game, an artist, a hobby, or topics like if Yoda really knew about Order 66 beforehand. We want to expand these opportunities to allow our communities to let new users find these spaces, which means we're here to help provide some guidance into some of the best ways to use these spaces and what is not allowed.

Note to Server Owners and Moderators

Since Stages will be spaces that exist within your server, server owners and stage moderators are responsible and accountable for the Stages being held. We empower and equip our communities to have the tools to help them properly ensure that these spaces are not engaging in any violations and are kept safe and welcoming. Stages are extensions of your server and activity that happens within them will be representative of your server. You'll have the ability to make your stage available only to members of your server or open to anyone on Discord. Public Stages have some different features and must follow additional requirements as described below.

Stage Guidelines:

1. Abide by the Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. This means that issues reported to your server should be addressed by your moderators and admins. Your moderator team should know when to escalate issues to Trust & Safety. Servers that violate Discord's Community Guidelines and Terms of Service will be subject to further action from our Trust & Safety Team.

  • We want Discord to be a safe, positive, and inclusive experience. Our Trust & Safety team will investigate Stages that are reported to us or that we proactively identify as likely in violation of our policies, and Trust & Safety team members may temporarily join a live Stage to investigate potential violations.

2. Respect people's intellectual property and other rights. Only incorporate content that you own or have a license to use. Do not invade anyone's privacy, libel them, or otherwise violate their rights.

    • Discord does not currently provide a recording or transcript feature. If you choose to use third-party tools to record or transcribe your event, you must make sure that you are following relevant laws, including getting consent from speakers and audience members if needed.

3. Foster a healthy and positive environment. People should feel welcome in your Stage. Create environments where people want to spend time with each other, share interests, participate in community events, and build friendships. Do not cultivate general toxic behavior, harassment of others, or other derogatory content.

4. Have a moderator team. Moderators can help ensure nothing rule-breaking is happening during your Stage events and can find meaningful ways for your members to engage. Build a moderator team that members of your community can trust and turn to for help. Note: Moderators will help facilitate your conversations in your Stage and should help enforce your server-specific rules as well!

5. Have a topic and description that accurately describes the Stage that is free of profanity. Help potential members understand why they want to join the Stage. The Stage title and description should accurately reflect the nature of the event, and not mislead users about who will be speaking or what will be discussed.

6. Do not host explicit, graphic, or sexual content. Explicit and age-restricted content is not allowed in Stages. Stages should be appropriate for audiences of all ages 13+.

7. Public Stages: Be mindful anyone can join your server while your public Stage is live. Though these Stages are extensions of your community, when you opt-in to make your Stage public, you are also temporarily making your server public while the event is live. This means that you should make sure that any and all sensitive channels are marked private and have the appropriate roles and permissions set up.

name: Mobile Voice Overlay (Android)
title: Mobile Voice Overlay (Android)
body:
Note: Beginning on August 1st, 2022, Discord users can expect to see improvements to the Discord Android application, including:
- Feature consistency across platforms through a centralized and streamlined app development process across Android, iOS and desktop
- Faster app update release cycles when a new feature is introduced or a pesky bug is fixed thanks to a more consolidated process
Over the next few weeks, the Android app will begin to transition to the React Native framework to enhance the user experience. To use the new version of the Discord app:
- Go to the Google Play Store to manually update your Discord app.
- Otherwise, if auto-update is enabled on your Android device, the app should automatically update.
You can read more about this change in our blog post.
The old Discord Android application will officially sunset on September 1st, 2022, so make sure you've updated your Android app from the Google Play Store before then!

Discord Mobile Voice Overlay is now on Android! Once enabled, whenever you're in an active voice call or channel on Discord, an overlay bubble will show up on your phone.

Tapping that bubble will expand to show what you see below!

Well, almost exactly what you see here if you have the same name and you have the same friends with the same avatars and you're playing the same game.


You will be able to see who's talking, who's in the call, and access shortcuts (speaker, mute, hang up) while using other apps—no need to switch back to Discord as this overlay will persist on your phone.

Don't want to see the bubble? You can drag it out at any time! Just touch the bubble and you should see an "X" at the bottom of your screen, then simply move the bubble to the "X" and it'll go away.

Note: Moving the bubble onto the "X" DOES NOT hang up the call. You will need to hang up explicitly by tapping on the hangup button within the expanded overlay or within Discord.

How to enable mobile voice overlay

Make sure you are on Discord Android Version 9.4.5. You can enable the Mobile Voice Overlay by going into Settings -> Voice & Video -> and you should see a "Enable Mobile Voice Overlay" toggle.

When you enable the toggle, you'll be taken to the Android System permissions to allow Discord to "draw on top". This permission is required to allow you to see the overlay while using other apps!


Tadaa, now you can use the mobile voice overlay!

name: Reduced Motion Setting
title: Reduced Motion Setting
body:
Discord uses motion effects to create the perception of depth. However, we understand that these effects can cause problems for users who are affected by excess motion and movement within apps. So, we're adding Reduced Motion to help!

What does this article cover? 

  • What does Reduced Motion do?
    • What Animations and Movement that are limited when Reduced Motion is enabled?
  • Where can I find this setting?
  • Windows 
    • Having Trouble Disabling Reduced Motion?
  • MacOS
  • iOS
  • Android

What does Reduced Motion do?

This setting is an accessibility feature that limits the amount and intensity of animations within Discord. 
 

Animations and Movement that are limited when Reduced Motion is enabled:

  • New/Old messages Bar & Jump to Messages - slide animation removed and instead send you directly to the message
  • Disables the shaking animation that happens when trying to close out setting pages that have unsaved changes.
  • Server banner animation is minimized when scrolling down a channel list.
  • Setting pages no longer fade in/out and instead instantly open/close.
  • Disable the message highlight that occurs when your mouse is hovering over a message in chat. 
  • Disables the background animations found on the Login/Authentication page.
  • Disables GIF avatars from playing in the chat unless you click into the user profile.
  • Animations for tooltips, menu dropdowns, and context/pop-out menus will now fade in. 
  • Discord's loading animation when launching (spinning Clyde) will now be static.
  • Animated Emojis will now be static in the Emoji Picker, within chat, statuses, and reactions:

Where can I find this setting?

You can find the setting by going to User Settings  ⟶ Appearance ⟶ Accessibility.
 
Currently, you can choose between: 
  • Sync with computer
  • Enable Reduced Motion

Sync with computer(default):

If you'd like Discord to automatically match the same settings that you have your computer's current settings, press on that "Sync with computer" button!

Enable Reduced Motion:

If you'd like to only enable Reduced Motion in Discord, but keep your current computer settings the same, you can instead toggle "Enabled Reduced Motion" on.

When this setting is enabled, Discord will reduce animations and movements within the app regardless of your system configurations. 

If you would like to disable Reduced Motion in Discord, simply toggle "Enabled Reduced Motion" off. 

Having Trouble Disabling Reduced Motion?

If you’re having trouble getting Reduced Motion to be disabled on Discord, it’s most likely due to pre-configured settings that have been enabled on your system.

For Mac OS, there’s one option, but for Windows, there are multiple settings that could enable Reduced Motion in Discord. We have steps below for where to look to double check on these settings.

To check your current system settings:

Windows

  • Display Settings
    • On Windows 10, go to Settings ⟶ Ease of Access ⟶ Display ⟶ Simplify and personalize Windows. Toggle "Show animation in Windows"  off.

  • Advanced System Settings
    • If you're still unable to disable Reduced Motion, you will need to open Advanced System Settings and make sure that the Animate controls and elements inside windows option checked!
    • This setting will cause Reduced Motion to enable, but you can adjust the individual animations that you prefer to keep disabled on your system within this menu.

Note: If you have motion and animation effects disabled on your system for reasons other than accessibility, then following the step above should allow you to disable Reduced motion for Discord, but enable for your system.

Mac

  • On a Mac, you go to System Preferences ⟶ Accessibility ⟶ Display and uncheck the box for "Reduce motion".

iOS

  • On iOS, The settings can be found in User Settings (Bottom right by pressing your Avatar) ⟶ App Settings ⟶ Appearance ⟶ Reduced Motion

Sync with Device Settings will make it so that the Discord app stays in sync with the Reduce Motion setting in iOS' accessibility settings: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT202655 

When reduced motion is enabled it will overwrite two other settings:

  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Automatically play GIFs when possible will be set to off and disabled
  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Play animated emoji will be set to off and disabled

Android

  • On Android, The settings can be found in User Settings (Bottom right by pressing your Avatar) ⟶ App Settings ⟶ Appearance ⟶ Reduced Motion

When reduced motion is enabled it will overwrite two other settings:

  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Automatically play GIFs when possible will be set to off and disabled
  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Play animated emoji will be set to off and disabled
  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Stickers Animate on interaction

Have Questions or Feedback?

We hope this update improves your Discord experience and if you would like to give our Accessibility team live feedback, please fill out this form: https://dis.gd/a11y. 

If you have any additional questions, please reach out to our support team here: https://dis.gd/contact or Tweet at us @discord!

name: Images Not Loading and Other Connection Errors
title: Images Not Loading and Other Connection Errors
body:
Having trouble seeing images and other attachments on Discord? Or, are you having trouble downloading or updating our app? There are a few things that could be causing the trouble, and we’re here to help!

Initial Troubleshooting Steps

As a first step, please try changing your DNS provider! 

DNS issues are the most common cause for images being broken and other connection troubles, and changing your DNS provider can potentially lead to faster and safer browsing! 

We’ve got a guide on how to change your DNS provider here.

UK Users

If you’re in the UK and your internet service provider is BT, the folks at British Telecom have confirmed that their DNS service is blocking images and other parts of our service for some users. BT has recommended that impacted users change their DNS provider. 

US Users

If changing your DNS provider doesn’t do the trick, and your internet service provider is Xfinity, we’ve become aware that Xfinity has blocked our image delivery services for users with xFi Routers who have Private Browsing enabled. 

We are working with Comcast to find a solution to this issue. In the meantime, we would recommend contacting Xfinity Support for additional help! https://www.xfinity.com/support/

All Regions and ISPs

If a DNS provider swap didn’t do the trick, we’re aware that some antivirus and security providers, such as Norton Family and Lookout, have blocked our services in the past. 

With that in mind, please try allowisting Discord in your antivirus software as a next step! You may need to contact your antivirus provider for support in allowlisting us.

name: How do I pin messages?
title: How do I pin messages?
body:
Where an announcements channel might not get the job done, Discord has a pin messages function that'll allow you to have quick access to important messages from way far back or as recently as you like.

 

Adding New Pins 

Ready your thumbtacks and start pinning away!

To pin a message, just click on the "three dots"/More icon at the far right of the message:

If your role has the Manage Messages permission (or you're the server owner), you'll see the "Pin Message" feature in the drop-down menu.

Right-clicking on the message will also work too!

 

Once you confirm that you want to pin the message, you will save that message to the pin window!

As the prompt says, make sure you double check for posterity and greatness. These aren't just any common messages, you know.

Note: You can only have 50 pins per channel/DM so make sure to pin your messages wisely!

Viewing All Pinned Messages

Collapsable Corkboard, Endless Time Warp:

Any pinned message will appear in the pin window, accessed by clicking the pin icon in the top-right corner:

Jumping to Pinned Message

Another important point is that no matter how long ago the pinned message is, you can click the "jump" link next to the pinned message in the pin window to jump all the way back to when that message was originally written:

Removing Pins

Removing pins when you no longer need them or need to delete old pins for more is also easy peasy! 

When you're ready to unpin a message, just click the "X" icon next to that "Jump" button we saw earlier:

And confirm:

Last Protip: 
By holding shift and clicking the "X" unpin icon in the pin window, you can bypass the above "kthx" unpinning message to unlock true rapid-fire unpinning madness.

name: Safety Resources for Australian Users
title: Safety Resources for Australian Users
body:
Creating a safe environment for our users is at the core of our mission at Discord. We share this commitment with regulators, safety partners and non-governmental organisations around the world.

The eSafety Commissioner in Australia plays a key role in empowering all Australians to have safer and more positive online experiences. As Australia’s dedicated online safety regulator, eSafety works together with the private sector to protect Australians from a range of online harms, from cyberbullying to the distribution of illegal material.

As part of our efforts to keep Discord safe, we want our Australian users to be aware of the ways in which eSafety can help them respond to the challenges they may encounter online. You can find out more information about eSafety on their website, including how to make a complaint.

In addition to these resources, Discord provides tools to help all users stay safe on the platform, like our Safety Center. If you are an Australian user seeking specific assistance with a suspected financial scam, you can report this to Discord by following the instructions in our Deceptive Practices Policy Explainer, and report the issue to your financial institution or local law enforcement.

eSafety’s website also includes a comprehensive list of counselling and support services tailored for Australians.

name: Age-Restricted Commands
title: Age-Restricted Commands
body:
What this article covers:

  • What are Age-Restricted Commands?
  • Who can use Age-Restricted Commands?
  • Where can they be used?
  • How do I access Age-Restricted Commands?
  • Help! I’m over 18 years old, but can’t use Age-Restricted commands!
    • What does Discord need to submit an appeal?

What are Age-Restricted Commands?

Age-restricted commands are commands from apps that may contain age-restricted content, and may only be used by people 18 or older. To ensure that Discord is safe for everyone, our policies require that developers label adult content as age-restricted and not distribute it to people under the age of 18.

Who can use Age-Restricted Commands?

Users who are 18 and older can access them in servers and DMs.

Where can they be used?

They can be used within age-restricted channels in servers, and in DMs after a user has opted-in to use them.

How do I access Age-Restricted Commands?

In servers, you can use these commands only within age-restricted channels. Not all apps have age-restricted commands, but if an app in your server has them, they’ll only be accessible within those designated channels.

In DMs, age-restricted commands are turned off by default. If an app contains age-restricted commands, you can access them by enabling the toggle within User Settings > Privacy> Server Privacy Defaults.

Help! I’m over 18 years old, but can’t use Age-Restricted commands!

If you are over the age of 18 and have been locked out of an age-restricted channel, or are unable to use age-restricted commands in DMs, you can appeal by following the instructions below. 

What does Discord need to submit an appeal?

Step 1: 

Take a photo of yourself that includes yourself holding the following items:

  1. A photo ID that contains your date of birth
  2. A piece of paper that shows your full Discord Username

Step 2: 

Once you have taken the photo, submit a request to the Trust & Safety team here: https://dis.gd/request and select “Appeals, age update, other questions” and then "Update my age information".

Note:

- All of the required information needs to be visible and readable in ONE photo.

- You must send the photo with the email address associated with your Discord account

The information you provide will only be used to verify your age and will not be used for any other purpose.

name: Discord Student Hubs Guidelines
title: Discord Student Hubs Guidelines
body:
Discord Hubs for Students allow students to verify their Discord account with their official student email, and unlock access to an exclusive hub for students at their school. Within the hub, they can connect with other verified students, discover servers for study groups or classes, and share their own servers for fellow students to join. 

Note to All Hub Members

Please be mindful that:

  • Hubs are not affiliated with or managed by a school or school staff.
  • Servers in a Hub are student-run but may include non-students.

Note to Server Owners and Moderators of Servers in a Hub

Server owners and moderators are responsible and accountable for their server's affiliation in a Student Hub. We empower and equip our communities to have the tools to help them properly ensure that these spaces are not engaging in any violations and are kept safe and welcoming. Student Hubs have some different features and servers must follow additional requirements as described below.

Student Hub Guidelines

1. Abide by the Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. This means that issues reported to your server should be addressed by your moderators and admins. Your moderator team should know when to escalate issues to Trust & Safety. Servers that violate Discord's Community Guidelines and Terms of Service will be subject to further action from our Trust & Safety Team.

  • We want Discord to be a safe, positive, and inclusive experience. Our Trust & Safety team will investigate Student Hubs that are reported to us or that we proactively identify as likely in violation of our policies, and Trust & Safety team members may temporarily join a Student Hub to investigate potential violations.
  • We may remove an affiliated server or account from the Student Hub if the server or account recently violated our Community Guidelines and received an enforcement action.

2. Foster a healthy and positive environment. People should feel welcome in your Student Hub and affiliated-server. Create environments where people want to spend time with each other, share interests, participate in community events, and build friendships. Examples include:

  • No content or behavior meant to single out, bully, or harass other students, faculty, or server members.
  • No discussions about controlled substances or drugs. This may get you reported to law enforcement.
  • No servers dedicated to using regulated goods, such as alcohol.
  • Do not cultivate general toxic behavior or other derogatory content.

3. Ensure academic honesty. No content or behavior promoting, facilitating, or conducting academic dishonesty, including cheating and plagiarism. Study groups and class discussions are allowed and highly recommended!

4. Do not host graphic or sexual content. Graphic violence and sexual content is not allowed in Student Hubs. Servers linked to Student Hubs should be appropriate for audiences of all ages 13+ and cannot include age-gated servers.

5. Have a server name and description that accurately describes the server that is free of profanity. Help potential members understand why they want to join the server you listed in your Student Hub.

6. Respect people's intellectual property and other rights. Only incorporate content that you own or have a license to use. Do not invade anyone's privacy, libel them, or otherwise violate their rights.

7. Have a moderator team. Moderators can help ensure nothing rule-breaking is happening in your Student Hub-affiliated server and can find meaningful ways for your members to engage. Build a moderator team that members of your community can trust and turn to for help.

We may consider off-platform behavior when assessing an account or server for violation of the Student Hub guidelines.

Enforcement

If you or your affiliated-Server violate any of the above guidelines, we may take any of the following enforcement actions:

  • Temporarily banning your server from the Student Hub until abides by the above guidelines.
  • Removing your server from the Student Hub permanently.
  • Temporarily banning your account from the Student Hub.
  • Removing your account and school email from being able to participate in the Student Hub.
  • Temporarily banning your account from Discord.

If your server or account is violating our Community Guidelines, you will receive additional enforcement actions, which include:

  • Removing violative content.
  • Warning an account/server.
  • Temporarily banning your account.
  • Permanently banning your account.
  • Temporarily banning a server.
  • Permanently banning your server.

name: Why isn't my DM going through?
title: Why isn't my DM going through?
body:
If your direct message was unable to be sent, you'll receive an error message from Clyde that states the following:

Your message could not be delivered. This is usually because you don't share a server with the recipient or the recipient is only accepting direct messages from friends.

Clyde’s message will look something like this:

Possible Reasons for This Error

There can be a few reasons why you are unable to send a direct message to someone. Here are possible reasons for the error that you may be encountering:

  • You don't share a server with the DM recipient.
  • You've disabled direct messages on your shared server.
  • You have not completed the required membership screening steps in your shared server.
  • The DM recipient is only accepting direct messages from friends.
  • You were blocked by the DM recipient.
If it seems you are running into a technical error when trying to send a DM, please reach out to our Discord Support team. Otherwise, the Discord Support team will not be able to provide further assistance.
For further information, please review our Blocking & Privacy article to learn more about these features.

name: Discord Partnership Code of Conduct
title: Discord Partnership Code of Conduct
body:
Partnered servers are at the forefront of the community. We want our Partnered servers to welcome all users, whether complete newcomers to Discord or expert users and longtime members. We look to our partners to provide a positive place for people to come together around their communities.

As a Partner, always remember to conduct yourself responsibly and treat others with respect, patience, and kindness. Whether you’re on-stream, chatting, or showing off the profile badge you’ve earned, your actions reflect on Discord itself.

We require owners, admins, and moderators in Partnered servers to uphold the rules in this Partner Code of Conduct and those detailed in our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. 

Failure to uphold these standards will lead to a warning, both through email and in the application itself, and a chance to correct the violation. If action is not taken on the reported content within 48 hours, we will take additional action, including removing the partnership status. Any further violations of the Partner Code of Conduct may also remove the partnership.

The following Code of Conduct outlines our requirements for Partnered servers.

I. BEHAVIOR AND ENGAGEMENT WITH USERS

As a Partner, always consider how others may perceive your statements. Even if you intend something as a joke, there may be others who do not see it as such.

This does not mean we will revoke the partnership if a user says something offensive in your server. We understand the challenges of moderating big servers — especially ones with users from all over the world. However, we expect you to build a moderation team that will take action on issues within a reasonable timeframe. Having no moderation or claiming the server is too big to moderate is unacceptable.

Partnered servers should be an example of the best communities that Discord offers, so we have a higher standard for the conversation and moderation of those servers. The following are prohibited in a partnered Discord:

  • Discriminatory jokes and hate speech (attacks on an individual or group based on their race, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, sexual orientation, religious affiliation, or disabilities)
  • Moderators or admins make verbal abuse, insults, and threats towards others or display offensive, derogatory, or explicit content.
  • Advocating for or encouraging any of the above behavior.
  • Selling a Partnered server or account is prohibited.

As a Discord Partner and a representative of Discord, you should be on good behavior on the Discord platform, across other social media platforms, and in real life. If we are made aware of situations where you are representing Discord poorly by, for example, violating other platforms' Terms of Service or acting in a manner that is unbecoming of a Discord Partner, we may rescind the Partner status. Without warning, we reserve the right to de-partner any community based on their behavior, both on and off Discord.

II. ADULT CONTENT GUIDELINES

Explicit pornographic content does not have a place in Partnered servers. This includes videos, gifs, or still images depicting explicit sexual actions, whether real or illustrated and detailed verbal descriptions of explicit sexual acts. The Discord Partners Program is designed to highlight awesome communities and content creators and generally be welcoming to those of all ages. 

However, conversations around adult topics are allowed — we understand that there are Partnered servers that deal with sensitive and difficult topics, and we welcome those conversations and communities. In those servers, those channels should be clearly marked and opt-in. 

III. REPRESENTATIONS AND MISREPRESENTATIONS

Servers are Partnered based on their content and community at the point of application and for what that community will likely grow into. That means we expect your Discord will continue to be about the subject you applied for.

  • If you (the partner) are a content creator, your server should be centered around your content. Switching to a community-based server will void your partnership. 
  • If you are a community server, your server’s focus should be the content under which you applied for partnership. Switching or repurposing the server from its original purpose will void your partnership.

In short, we don’t appreciate a bait-and-switch. It’s totally understandable if you are a content creator and change from one game to another, but it’s less reasonable if you’re a community around RPGs and one day you delete all channels and change to be about your interest in football or vice versa.

Finally, you (the partner) must maintain ownership of your partnered Discord server to stay in the program. If you delete or transfer ownership for any reason without communication to Discord, your partnership, and all Discord perks will be revoked. 

IV. MAINTAINING QUALITY CONTENT

Content creators or communities are expected to create original content. Complete copying or plagiarizing another party’s content will result in immediate removal from the partner program. We want our Partnered servers to reflect active Discord communities and users well. 

Please note: We have the right to update this Code of Conduct at any time, and as Discord evolves, so may our expectations for our Partners. If this Code of Conduct changes, we'll communicate those changes to you (the partner) accordingly. 

As a Discord Partner, always remember to conduct yourself responsibly and treat others the way you’d like to be treated. We want to ensure that you are a shining example of the best parts of the platform and a prime example that other users should strive to be. Be the awesome you want to see in the world.

name: [macOS] Install and Updating Errors
title: [macOS] Install and Updating Errors
body:
Hey, listen! If you're having issues updating or installing Discord on your shiny Macintosh machine, we can help! Though not intentional, there are various issues that can cause the install or update process to fail. You'll see this as an endless update, or an unexplained install error! In cases like these, completely reinstalling Discord will often improve our updater's performance and clear out any issues. Follow these steps!

Note: Remember that Discord only supports MacOS 10.11 and up (El Capitan) or above! Also, if you're running macOS on a machine that wasn't produced by Apple (IE, a Hackintosh), you may run into unique issues!

Reinstalling Discord

  • Close Discord by using ⌘+Q or selecting the Quit option from the menubar, then make sure all Discord processes are terminated from within your Mac's Activity Monitor. (You can quickly launch the Activity Monitor by using Spotlight or Siri on your Mac!) 

  • Delete the 2 following folders:
    1. ~/Library/Application Support/Discord
    2. /Library/Application Support/Discord

To find those folders, open Finder, press ⇧⌘+G (or Go > Go to Folder in the menubar), and enter:

~/Library/Application Support in the window and hit enter: 

 Then /Library/Application Support in the run window and hit enter:


In both of these cases, find the Discord folders in these files and drag them to your Trash. Note: There may not be a Discord folder in the second file (/Library/Application Support). If there isn't, that's okay!

Next, open your Applications folder. Find Discord and drag it to your Trash. Finally, empty your Trash!

If your OS tells you that the file cannot be deleted because it's still in use. Open up the Activity Monitor and terminate all instances of Discord.

  • Restart your system.
  • Reinstall via https://discord.com/api/download?platform=osx

Note: Make sure that all instances of Discord are closed out before attempting these steps!

Diagnosing Network Issues

If reinstalling Discord doesn't do the trick, it's possible your network configuration is preventing our updater from doing its job! To clear up any networking issues, there's some basic troubleshooting steps you should try!

First, try setting your DNS to Google Public DNS!

  • Open System Preferences from your Mac's Apple menu, then select Network. From there, choose the network you're currently using (for example, Wi-Fi)
  • Select Advanced..., select the DNS tab in the top bar, then use the Plus button under DNS Servers to add the following DNS server options!
    • 8.8.8.8
    • 8.8.4.4
    • 2001:4860:4860::8888
    • 2001:4860:4860::8844
  • Click OK, then close System Preferences and try relaunching Discord!

If that doesn't do the trick, try renewing your Mac's IP address! 

  • Open System Preferences from your Mac's Apple menu, then select Network. From there, choose the network you're currently using (for example, Wi-Fi)
  • Select Advanced..., then select the TCP/IP tab
  • Click Renew DHCP Lease
  • Select OK, close System Preferences, then try relaunching Discord once more!

Note: If none of these steps do the trick, reach out to our Support Team at https://dis.gd/contact

name: New Mobile App Updates & Layout
title: New Mobile App Updates & Layout
body:
Hello there! If you’ve been using Discord for a while now, you probably noticed the mobile app was designed to reflect the desktop app. With this new iteration of Discord on mobile, we hope to make the mobile experience feel like it was optimized for your mobile device rather than a scaled-down desktop app. The new mobile design aims to simplify and improve the Discord experience for everyone by creating a more organized, streamlined, and better-looking mobile app that helps you get to your chats quickly and easily. 

We’re actively gathering feedback as we release this change to ensure that we continue to provide the best experience on Discord. For those of you who have already experienced previous iterations of our mobile app, thank you for all the thoughtful feedback you've shared with us so far! We've been paying great attention to it and it's helping us continue to make improvements. If you’re new to this version of the app, be sure to explore the new mobile experience and all that it has to offer. If something doesn’t work for you, please let us know so we can continue to improve! 

This Help Center article will explain the core updates to the mobile app and how you can provide feedback and thoughts on what does or doesn’t work for you.

What this article covers:

  • Home Tab for your Messages and Servers
  • Messages Icon
    • Active Now
    • Favorite DMs and Group Chats
    • DM and Group Chat Details Page
    • DM and Group Chat Creation
    • Add Friends
  • Notifications Tab
  • You Tab
    • Friends List
    • Settings & Settings Search
  • Voice & Video Calls
  • Swipe to Reply
  • Accessing Channel, DM, or Group Chat Details
  • New Customization Options
    • Themes
    • Message Previews
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Home Tab for your Messages and Servers

The Home tab, located in the bottom-left corner of the app, is where you can find all your servers and access your Direct Messages (DMs) and group chats.

Once you open the Home tab, you’ll see the Messages icon and all of your servers on the left of the screen. Tapping on the Messages icon will show all the DMs and group chats you’re part of. Tapping on a server will open it within the Servers tab and allow you to scroll through and open that server’s channels.

In each of your servers, you’ll be able to Favorite channels, use the search bar at the top of the server channel list to find messages and content in a server, and see the channel details of each server channel, which includes a list of the server members in that channel, the Media/Files/Links sent in that channel, the threads created, and more.

Messages Icon

Your DMs and group chats can now be accessed by tapping on the Messages icon [] at the top left corner of the server list. 

You can also search across all of your DMs and group chats to find the chat you’re looking for selecting the search icon [].

Active Now

While in Messages, you can easily see what your friends are up to within the Active Now section. Active Now can show things such as:

  • When your friends are currently in a Voice Channel in a mutual server
  • A game your friend is playing
  • If your friend is participating in any activity that supports Rich Presence, like listening to Spotify or watching something on Crunchyroll
  • Your friend’s Status, including their Custom Status

Learn more about your own Activity Status settings here.

Favorite DMs And Group Chats

You can favorite direct messages (DMs) and group chats so that they stay pinned to the top of your Messages tab for quicker access. 

1. To favorite a DM or group chat, tap on the Home tab > Messages icon.  

2. While in Messages, navigate to the DM or group chat you would like to favorite. 

3. Then, long-press it to open the options menu where you can tap Favorite. 

You will then see the DM or group chat at the top of your messages with a star icon [] next to it.

You can repeat the same process and select Unfavorite to remove a G/DM from your favorites. 

DM And Group Chat Details Page

From this page, you can search for messages sent in the DM or group chat, see its members and their statuses, and filter for the media, GIFs, files, and links shared there. 

You could also use this page to find a specific photo that you sent, but don’t remember when you sent it. By selecting the Media filter, you can browse all of the images and videos sent in that DM or group chat quickly without having to scroll through the whole chat history.

DM And Group Chat Creation

From the Home tab > Messages, you can press the blurple Message button [] in the bottom right of the screen to start a new DM or group chat. 

From here, you can type the names of your friends that you want to add or tap on their profiles to add them to the chat.

Once everyone is there, you can then tap on the text box at the bottom of the screen to begin sending a message. If you have an existing group chat with the users selected for the chat, you will automatically see that group chat instead of starting a new one. 

If you do want to create a new group, just select New Group at the top of the screen before selecting any friends.

Add Friends

You can add new friends by heading over to the Home tab > Messages icon and tapping the Add Friends button. 

Notifications Tab

We simplified your notifications experience to emphasize the things you can uniquely find in the Notifications tab, like friend requests.

All notifications in the Notifications tab are actionable: Join an event, message someone who just accepted your friend request, etc. 

You no longer need to click a notification for it to be considered read in the Notifications tab, just seeing it is enough. The next time you return to the Notifications tab, all read notifications will be de-emphasized and new notifications will be emphasized so you always know what’s new and don’t have to actively clear your notifications. 

Red badges will persist on the Notifications tab when you have pending friend requests, and you must resolve your pending friend requests to clear them.

You Tab

The You tab is your dedicated space to view and customize how you appear to others on Discord. You can find the You tab in the bottom right corner of the app. From this tab, you can easily edit your profile, set your status, view your friends, or manage your settings. 

Friends List

We moved the Friends list to be in the You tab. To see your existing friends, view pending friend requests, and add new friends, tap Your Friends in the You tab. Only you can see your Friends list.

Settings & Settings Search

App Settings are still in this tab and you can now access them by tapping the gear icon at the top right of the You tab. If you want to get to settings quickly, you can also double-tap the You tab icon at the bottom of the screen.

You can now search within Settings. It’s a small but mighty improvement. Now, you don't have to waste time scrolling through every single setting to find what you're looking for. Simply type in the search bar and watch the magic happen.

Voice & Video Calls

We’ve updated the interface for voice and video calls. Before joining a voice call, you can easily preview the Text in Voice for that call without joining the call by tapping the quote icon to the right of the Join Voice button. Tap the microphone icon to the left of the Join Voice button to control whether you will enter the call muted or unmuted. You must tap the Join Voice button to enter a voice call.

 

Instead of opening the details and settings for a voice call, swiping up from the bottom of the screen now opens the Text in Voice chat for that voice call. 

To find the details and settings for a voice call, tap the name of the voice call at the top of the screen. See below for the function of each button at the top of a voice call:

 

1. Minimize voice call within Discord

2. Open call details and settings

3. Change audio to speakerphone

4. Invite friends to call

To screenshare or start an activity, tap on the screen to reveal the bottom menu. Then you can tap on the rocket icon to pull up all available activities.

When in a voice call, you can double-tap on another user’s tile to make their video fullscreen. 

When you're in a fullscreen activity or stream, double-tap to minimize it and get back to the rest of the call participants.

Swipe to Reply

We added swipe-to-reply on messages for faster witty retorts. Simply swipe from right to left across a message in a DM or channel to reply to that message. 

Accessing Channel, DM, or Group Chat Details

Previously, swiping from right to left across a channel, DM, or group chat would take you to see the details of that chat such as pinned messages or a list of who is in the channel, DM, or group chat. To access channel, DM, or group chat details, tap on the name of the channel, DM, or group chat at the top of the screen.

New Customization Options

We’ve added more ways to make the Discord mobile app feel like your space through customization options. We added a new Midnight theme and the ability to toggle message previews in your Messages tab.

Themes

We added the new Midnight theme, which is pure black to go easy on your eyes and save battery on OLED compatible devices. 

1. You can choose your theme by navigating to your Settings.

2. Select Appearance.

3. Then go to THEME and select your desired theme. 

You can also toggle on Sync across clients to have your themes stay consistent across your desktop and mobile apps. 

Midnight theme is currently not available on Desktop.

Message Previews

Make every unread DM a total surprise when you turn off message previews for added privacy and a more simplified chat look. To update your message preview preferences:

1. Navigating to your Settings.

2. Select Appearance.

3. Go to Message Previews and update your preferences.

Frequently Asked Questions 

Q: Can I get the new mobile app updates and layout?

A: We are currently rolling out the latest updates to our mobile app, including the new layout, to all of our users, but it may take some time for you to be enrolled. Please continue to make sure that your app is up to date with the latest version from the app store. When you become eligible for the new mobile app experience, you will be notified within the app.

Q: Why are you changing the mobile app layout?

A: We’re always looking for ways to improve our users’ experience on Discord and a big part of this is making investments in improving and evolving the features available on mobile.

Q: Are there iOS/OS or Discord app version requirements (ie. iOS 11.0+, Android 5.0+, Discord version 206+)?

A: You must have the latest version of the Discord app to experience these updates. We also recommend that you have the latest version of your mobile device’s OS.

Q: Were there any changes to the layout of the Settings page?

A: Yes, the location has changed and we have added a search bar to Settings. You can find your Settings page in the You tab on the bottom right of the app via the gear icon in the top right of the You tab. If you want to get to settings quickly, you can also double-tap the You tab icon at the bottom of the screen to jump to Settings.

Q: Can I go back to the original mobile app layout?

A: We understand the change might take some getting used to, and we're here to help make that transition as smooth as possible for you. But with this update, the original mobile layout is no longer available.

Q: Will this be available for both Android and iOS users?

A: Yes.

Q: How do I find the details and members of a channel, DM, or group chat now that I cannot swipe to see it?

A: You can access channel, DM, or group chat details by tapping the name of a channel, DM, or group chat at the top of the chat.

name: Discord Soundboard Guide: Using, Adding, and Managing Sounds
title: Discord Soundboard Guide: Using, Adding, and Managing Sounds
body:
Soundboard is a Discord feature that you can use in voice channels with friends to react to conversations and video streams with brief audio clips.

Learn more about how you can use soundboard, add sounds to your soundboard, and how to manage soundboard usage in Discord servers.

What this article covers:
  • What is Soundboard?
    • Server Boost Soundboard
  • How do I use Soundboard?
    • How to Use Discord Soundboard on Desktop
    • How to Use Discord Soundboard on Mobile
    • How to Add Sounds to Discord Soundboard
  • As a Server Admin, How Can I Manage Soundboard?
    • How to Give or Remove the Use Soundboard permission
    • How to Manage Sounds for Soundboard
  • Soundboard Entrance Sounds
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is Soundboard?

Example of using the Soundboard sound “Quack”

What’s that sound? Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it’s your friend smashing the button with the airhorn sound in the server’s Soundboard! Soundboard is your way to react in a Discord voice channel with brief audio clips. Soundboard is a voice channel feature that allows you to play a short audio clip that can be heard by all participants in the same voice channel. Much like Reactions and Super Reactions, Soundboard is a way for you to express yourself and react to the voice channel’s conversation or Go Live stream.

Server Boost Soundboard

Servers have 8 preloaded sound slots for server members to start using Soundboard. Additional slots can be unlocked based on the server’s tier level with Server Boosting.

Tier 1: 24 slots

Tier 2: 35 slots

Tier 3: 48 slots

How do I use Soundboard?

How to Use Discord Soundboard on Desktop

1. Navigate to a server and join your intended voice channel.

2. While in the voice channel, you should see a confetti icon on the bottom-right if Soundboard is enabled for this voice channel. Press on the icon to open Soundboard. If a user is deafened in the channel, they will not hear the sound play.

Open Soundboard button while connected to a voice channel

3. Another way to access Soundboard when in a voice channel is by pressing the Soundboard icon in the bottom left of the Discord app.

Soundboard panel with all available sounds

4. With Soundboard open, you can hover over any available sound and then press the Play icon to play that sound. Pressing Play will play the sound for everyone in the voice channel to hear.

Play icon to play a sound

5. If there’s a sound you really like, you can also press on the Star icon to favorite a sound. To preview a sound and only play it for yourself, press the speaker icon.

How to Use Discord Soundboard on Mobile

1. Navigate to a server and join your intended voice channel.

2. While in the voice channel, tap on the screen to reveal a toolbar at the bottom of the screen.  From there, drag the toolbar upwards and tap the Soundboard option at the top of the menu.

3. After tapping the Soundboard option, you will see a list of available servers and sounds that you can use. Tap on any sound that you’d like to play.

Using Soundboard sounds on mobile

How to Add Sounds to Discord Soundboard

Info: You can only upload to Soundboard through desktop or browser.

To upload new sounds, press on the Add Sound button in the open Soundboard panel .

Upload a Sound panel

Please keep in mind that it’s your responsibility to ensure that any sounds you upload does not violate our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines, including ensuring that or "any sounds you upload do not infringe on the intellectual property rights of others.

As a Server Admin, how can I manage Soundboard?

How to Give or Remove the Use Soundboard Permission

To manage who can use Soundboard in your server, you can enable or disable the Use Soundboard permission for specific roles or server members.

Soundboard permission setting under Server Settings

You can manage this on a server-wide level by going to Server Settings, going to the Roles tab, selecting the desired role you want to customize, and toggle the Use Soundboard permission.

You can also manage this for individual voice channels by selecting Edit Channel for your intended voice channel, going to the Permissions tab, selecting the desired role or server member whose permissions you want to customize, and toggle the Use Soundboard permission.   

How to Manage Sounds for Soundboard in a Server

Soundboard tab under Server Settings

To manage the current Soundboard on your server head to Server Settings > Soundboard and you can edit or remove any current sounds listed.

Where to edit or remove Soundboard sounds

To remove any of the current uploaded sounds you can do so by pressing the “x” button next to a sound.

Users will only be able to edit or remove custom sounds from a server if they have Manage Expressions permission enabled for their role. To give a role this permission, head to Server Settings > Roles and then enable or disable it per role under Permissions.

Manage Expressions setting allows users to edit or remove sounds

For users to be able to add custom sounds to a server, they will need to have Create Expressions permission enabled for their role. To give a role this permission, head to Server Settings > Roles and then enable or disable it per role under Permissions.

Create Expressions setting allows users to add custom sounds

Soundboard Entrance Sounds

Are you finding yourself using a specific sound in Soundboard anytime you join a specific server? You can now set your own sound to automatically play from the Soundboard when you join a voice channel if you are a Nitro subscriber. 

1. To set it up, tap on User Settings, head to Voice & Video, then tap on the Soundboard selection

2. Under Sound Effects you can tap on the pencil icon to set a sound for all servers or customize your sounds per server.

3. To set a sound per server, tap on the drop down menu and select the server. With the server selected, tap on the pencil icon and select the soundboard sound you’d like to use.

4. Once your chosen sound is selected, tap on the X in the upper right corner to close and it’ll automatically save. 

How to set a Soundboard Entrance Sound

Now when you join a server voice channel, that sound will automatically play!

Tip: If you join a voice channel with your mic muted and Soundboard enabled, your entrance sound will play. If you join a voice channel in deafened mode, your entrance sound will not play.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How can I change the volume or opt out for Soundboard?

Volume control for Soundboard sounds

A: To change the volume of hearing Soundboard Sounds, please head to User Settings > Voice & Video > Soundboard > Soundboard Volume to adjust the slider to their preferred volume. This setting will sync across all devices. If set to 0%, you will not hear any sounds.

Q: Is there a keybind for Soundboard for the game overlay on Windows?

A: For Windows only, CTRL + ` is the Soundboard keybind to easily use Soundboard from within the game overlay.

Q: Can any server’s Soundboard sounds be used in other servers?

A: In order to use Soundboard sounds across servers, you need to have an active Nitro subscription. You do not need Nitro in order to use the Soundboard within the server itself.

name: Discord’s Brand Partnership Guidelines
title: Discord’s Brand Partnership Guidelines
body:
Discord was designed to bring people together. It is our hope that users on our platform are able to meaningfully connect with others around common interests. Partnerships with individuals, organizations, or brands can greatly assist our effort to create belonging based on the partners our users care about.

We expect those partners and our revenue sources to meet the standards of our values, specifically integrity, impact, and compassion, and policies, such as our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. We created this policy to articulate what kinds of partnerships we prohibit, consideration we will have when partnering, and ways to mitigate issues that may arise.

Partners are companies/entities that our community, talent, BD, branded communities teams directly engage with to support them in the creation or maintenance of a server on our platform.

Thus, Discord prohibits partners who:

  • Inconsistent with our Policies:
    • Target those under 13 years of age.
    • Infringe on someone else’s copyright, trademark, or intellectual property.
    • Engage or attempt to engage in any transaction involving controlled or regulated substances
    • Promote gambling, especially to minors.
    • Conduct harmful off-platform behaviors related to credible violent extremism, violent threats, and child abuse.
    • Promote hate speech or hateful conduct.
    • Share violence and gore with the intent to harass or shock non-consensually.
  • Inconsistent with our Values:
    • Promote pharmaceutical products or specific healthcare services, such as diet products.
    • Spread misinformation around COVID-19, vaccines, climate change denial, or election information.
    • Share or focus on sexually explicit content.
    • Conduct illegal or unethical business practices.
    • Promote the sale, exchange, or building of weapons and weapon accessories.

Additional considerations for partnership, such as a partners’ commitments to diversity, equity, & inclusion, human rights, and sustainability, are included. Policy also suggested mitigations of potentially prohibiting content for account managers to get their partners to compliance.

Our Values

Values are quite simply the behaviors that we value in ourselves and the partners we would with. These are the fundamental truths that we hold which guide our decision making and behavior in all our work, especially with the brands, organizations, individuals, and causes we associate ourselves to. 

The values we hold ourselves to are integrity, collaboration, excellence, impact, speed, transparency, and compassion. Of our values, we will focus on ensuring partners have integrity, have a positive impact, and are compassionate.

  • Integrity: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; moral uprightness.
    • We have always believed that being honest, honoring commitments, and doing what's morally right in the long run is the best way to live life, even when it's painful in the short term.
  • Impact: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another
    • We want our time on this Earth to mean something. We want to contribute to improving the human condition, and be a force for good by doing something that leaves the world a little bit better than we found it. This means a relentless focus on what is true, what matters, and building value over time through compounding leverage.
  • Compassion: Empathy and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.
    • We are all human and with that comes all the challenges and tribulations of life. Work takes up a lot of time for most of us, but is it not the entirety of our experiences. In order to show up and give our mission its all, people need to be able to be themselves - both on good days and bad. Let's not force people to be half of themselves. Instead, let's be mindful and supportive of each other, knowing that we all are striving to do the best for ourselves, our families, our company, and our communities.

Our Policies

In addition to Partnership Guidelines, Partners must follow Discord’s Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, and all the policies on our Help Center governing our service. Please take a moment to review them.  

Overall, Discord and our partners, their accounts, and their servers should be in compliance with our policies, aligned with our values, and a Force for Good for our users in the communities they live. 

Partnership Policy

Prohibit Content or Purposes

Below are prohibited content and partner purposes. If a partner violates any of the below, they cannot partner with Discord. There are some types of prohibitions that can be mitigated, so please check the Mitigations section for more information. 

  • Age: Discord prohibits inappropriate content targeting minors and users under 13.
    • Inappropriate content based on targeted user age.
      • For example: Alcohol content, sexually explicit content, etc for minors.  
    • Under 13 year olds
      • No partners or their products that feature children under 13 or primarily target children under 13 for their product. A child-related brand, like a children’s TV network, can be a partner if the content in the server is NOT designed to reach or market to under 13.
  • Community Guidelines: Discord prohibits content or activity within the partner’s server or account that violate our Community Guidelines.
    • Past Violations: We should not partner with accounts or servers that have violated our Community Guidelines.
      • If a partner’s account or server violated any of our highest harm Commuinity Guideslines (Violent Extremism, Violent Threats, or Child Sexual Abuse) in the past, they cannot partner with us.
      • If a partner’s account or server violated any of our other Community Guidelines in the last 3 months, they cannot partner with us until 3 months has passed or they express regret and rehabilitation.
  • Copyright & Trademark: Discord prohibits the infringement on others’ copyright, trademark,  intellectual property rights, or that promotes the sale of counterfeit goods.
  • Controlled & Illegal Substances: Discord prohibits the sale, buying, trading, or organizing the distribution of controlled, regulated, or illegal substances through our service. We define a controlled substance as any drug or chemical compound that is controlled or otherwise regulated by the US federal government.  A non-exhaustive list of such goods includes: alcohol, tobacco (including vaping products), marijuana, pharmaceuticals without a prescription, narcotics, and other drugs.
    • Discussion of legal, controlled substances is allowed in age-restricted spaces.
  • Gambling Content: Discord prohibits the promotion of gambling content. We define gambling content as placing bets or wagers on games of chance for prizes with real-world value. Discussions of gambling and gambling themes do not by themselves constitute a violation of this policy. Special consideration should be given in instances of suspected gambling that appear to target vulnerable populations (e.g., minors, at-risk gamblers) or that feature forms of addictive gameplay.
  • Harmful Off-Platform Behaviors: If we become aware of specific off-platform high harm activities with credible evidence committed by a Discord user, we will take the reported off-platform harmful activities into account when assessing a partnership.
    • This policy applies to our highest harm Community guidelines: Violent Extremism, Violent Threats, and Child Sexual Abuse.
  • Hateful Content: Discord prohibits the user or promotion of hate speech or hateful conduct. We define hate speech as any form of expression that denigrates, vilifies, or dehumanizes; promotes intense, irrational feelings of enmity (“hatred”); or incites harm against people on the basis of protected characteristics. This includes the use of hate symbols as well as claims casting doubt on mass atrocities.
  • Specific Healthcare Products: Discord prohibits the promotion of all pharmaceutical products and services, and some healthcare products and services. Restrictions are based on the specific product or service being promoted, as well as the country that the campaign is targeting.
    • Diet products: A partner cannot be focused on or promote a product focused on dieting, losing weight, or miracle cures for obesity. This content is sensitive and can promote disordered eating and self-harm.
  • Misinformation: Discord prohibits the sharing of some types of  false or misleading information (otherwise known as misinformation). Content that is false, misleading, and can lead to significant risk of physical or societal harm may not be shared on Discord. We specifically prohibit:
    • Health misinformation, particularly vaccine misinformation or COVID misinformation.
    • Climate change deniers and misleading information.
    • Election misinformation, including incorrect information around voting registration requirements, due dates for registration, and date or logistics related to voting day.
  • Sexually Explicit Content: Discord prohibits the partnership with partners who primarily produce or are trying to promote a specific server featuring sexually explicit content. Sexually explicit content is defined as simulated, drawn, or real media (images, audio, video) or text of pornography, sexual acts (including with sex toys), full nudity, implied nudity, and soliciting or offering sexual services. This content is shared with the explicit and exclusive purpose of sexual arousal.
  • Illegal or Unethical Business Practices: Discord prohibits partnering with individuals, organizations, or brands with a history of illegal or unethical business practices.
